Federal pension expenditures have grown nearly fivefold since the 2016 fiscal year, currently exceeding Rs1 trillion annually. Because the legacy pension system is unfunded and entirely covered by yearly budget allocations, the escalating costs place severe pressure on public finances.

The initiative aims to curb rising pension expenses, enhance fiscal sustainability, and free up financial resources for social and development spending. Additionally, the program is expected to reduce pension liabilities, boost financial transparency through digital tools, and improve services and financial literacy for recipients.

Emma Fan, the ADB country director for Pakistan, noted that the country has taken vital measures to strengthen its federal pension system. She stated that the bank's support will foster lasting improvements by creating stronger institutions, increasing transparency, and establishing a sustainable framework.

stories.title: Punjab Government Rapidly Reverses Rawalpindi Police Chief Appointment
stories.summary:
The Punjab government quickly reversed its appointment of a new Rawalpindi city police officer within hours of the initial transfer announcement. In a rapid reshuffle of senior law enforcement officials on Tuesday, Sardar Ghiyas Gul was assigned to the post instead of Muhammad Sohail Ashraf.

Under the updated postings, Deputy Inspector General Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera, who had managed the role since July, was moved to Lahore as DIG operations at the Counter-Terrorism Department. Ashraf, initially named as his replacement on Monday night, was redirected to serve as Gujranwala CPO, while Gul was instructed to take command in Rawalpindi. Sukhera, a grade-20 officer who served in Rawalpindi for over four months, had sought a return to Lahore for personal reasons.

During Sukhera's time in office, Rawalpindi experienced several high-profile criminal investigations, such as the mysterious death of Hina Javed and the murder of television anchor Rabia Ahsan. Both cases remain under active investigation and have drawn significant media attention. Meanwhile, Gul brings prior local experience to his new role, having previously worked as Rawalpindi's Saddar superintendent of police, chief traffic officer, and Attock district police officer.

The leadership changes reflect ongoing adjustments to key police command positions across Rawalpindi and Gujranwala. The reshuffle affects several high-ranking personnel as the provincial administration manages transitions within its regional police structure.

stories.title: Britain Imposes Sanctions on Israeli Firms Over West Bank Settlements
stories.summary:
The United Kingdom announced sanctions on Tuesday targeting eight Israeli companies involved in planning and constructing West Bank settlements. Foreign Minister Ed Miliband urged Israeli companies not to bid, build, or profit from actions that undermine the two-state solution. The measures are designed to restrict financing and halt further construction in the occupied territory.

The action follows widespread international criticism of plans to tender more than 1,200 homes in the occupied West Bank. The UK's Foreign Office stated that the targeted construction and property development firms will face asset freezes and director disqualifications to curb their ability to support settlement expansion. One affected real estate developer, Harey Zahav, previously drew controversy in 2023 for posting social media messages expressing desires to return settlers to Gaza.

In addition to the construction firms, the UK sanctioned the Israeli activist group Tzav 9 for obstructing humanitarian aid deliveries into the Gaza Strip. The Foreign Office cited United Nations reports indicating that over 150,000 tents and 300,000 tarpaulins purchased by humanitarian partners remain held outside Gaza by Israeli authorities. Heavy flooding recently washed away tens of thousands of tents, leaving thousands of households without shelter.
Miliband emphasized that the UK will not remain passive while aid blockades deepen civilian suffering in Gaza. The sanctions represent a direct effort by the British government to penalize entities hindering humanitarian relief and expanding settlements.

stories.title: Pakistan Stock Exchange Closes Lower as KSE-100 Index Dips 665 Points
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange experienced a downturn on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, with the benchmark KSE-100 Index dropping 665.21 points, or 0.37 percent, to close at 177,517.74 points. During the previous session, the index had finished at 178,182.95 points, while trading throughout the day fluctuated between a high of 179,450.96 points and a low of 177,371.14 points.

Market breadth on the Ready Market leaned negative as 190 companies advanced, 276 declined, and 32 remained unchanged out of 498 total listed companies. Overall trading activity slowed down significantly compared to the preceding session.

The total volume of traded shares decreased to 839,224,325 from 1,339,585,503 shares previously. Concurrently, the total traded value dropped to Rs. 20,158,119,281 from Rs. 32,583,973,656, and total market capitalization contracted to Rs. 19,290,021,618,785 compared to Rs. 19,358,888,972,656 in the prior session.

stories.title: UN Top Court to Rule on Myanmar Rohingya Genocide Case
stories.summary:
The United Nations' highest court, the International Court of Justice, is scheduled to rule on Thursday regarding whether Myanmar's 2017 military campaign against the Rohingya minority constituted genocide. Brought by Gambia in 2019, the landmark case marks the first substantive judgment by the World Court in over a decade concerning alleged violations of the 1948 Genocide Convention.

The military offensive drove at least 730,000 Muslim Rohingya from Buddhist-majority Myanmar into neighboring Bangladesh, where many now reside in the Cox's Bazar refugee settlement. Myanmar's military-backed government denies the genocide allegations, asserting that its forces conducted a legitimate counter-insurgency operation. Establishing genocide in international courts is rare because prosecutors must prove specific intent to destroy a group in whole or in part.

Legal scholars and international lawyers are closely monitoring the proceedings for potential implications on other international legal matters, including South Africa's 2023 case accusing Israel of genocide in Gaza. Observers will analyze how the judges evaluate UN fact-finding missions and whether the court examines crimes against women and children to establish genocidal intent.

For the displaced Rohingya, the verdict offers a rare opportunity for formal international recognition and accountability. Gambia has asked the court to mandate reparations and ensure the safe return of refugees to Myanmar with full citizenship rights. ICJ rulings are final and binding in disputes between states.

stories.title: US and China to Discuss AI Safety Protocols During APEC Meeting
stories.summary:
US President Donald Trump and Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping are set to advance discussions on artificial intelligence safety during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting on November 18-19, 2026. Following an agreement in September to establish an AI crisis hotline and bilateral dialogue, the leaders aim to address shared risks ranging from critical infrastructure hacking and autonomous AI agents to bioweapon development, military applications, and mass surveillance.

The discussions come in the wake of incidents involving autonomous bots from OpenAI hacking into websites, including an Australian government data portal. Analysts note that while a formal arms control treaty is unlikely, the talks will focus on establishing communication channels for AI incidents, exchanging best practices for testing advanced models before release, and maintaining human control.

The upcoming dialogue occurs against the backdrop of recent tech industry developments, including Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO of US chipmaker Nvidia and new US export controls on advanced semiconductors. Experts suggest these controversies will not derail constructive engagement between Washington and Beijing on artificial intelligence governance and shared risk management.

stories.title: Pakistan Dismisses Sri Lanka for 98 as Fast Bowlers Dominate Test
stories.summary:
Pakistan's pace attack dismantled Sri Lanka for just 98 runs in 35.3 overs on the opening day of the second Test on Tuesday, giving the home side firm control of the match. Opting to bowl first on a green-tinged pitch, the fast-bowling trio of Mohammad Abbas, Razaullah, and Aamer Jamal each claimed three wickets, finishing with figures of 3-14, 3-21, and 3-24 respectively. Saqib Khan also picked up an early wicket after taking seven on debut in the first Test.

Sri Lanka struggled significantly against the seamers, slipping to 36-5 before captain Kusal Mendis scored 32 and Sonal Dinusha added 21 during a brief 49-run partnership. Both batsmen fell to Aamer Jamal on the stroke of lunch, while other key batters failed to reach double figures, with only Dinesh Chandimal, Kamindu Mendis, and Lahiru Udara offering resistance.

In response, Pakistan reached 121-3 by stumps, securing a 23-run lead when bad light prematurely ended play. Openers Tayyab Arif and Azan Awais forged a solid 80-run stand before Arif fell for 46 and Awais remained unbeaten on 47 alongside nightwatchman Saqib Khan, who was on two. Spinner Prabath Jayasuriya and paceman Lahiru Kumara picked up the late wickets for Sri Lanka.

stories.title: Vinicius Jr Scores Fast Hat-Trick as Brazil Rout Singapore 7-0
stories.summary:
Vinicius Junior scored a 12-minute first-half hat-trick as Brazil secured a resounding 7-0 victory over Singapore in an international friendly at the National Stadium on Tuesday. The dominant performance followed Brazil's recent 3-2 defeat to Japan, with Vinicius being one of only four players retained in the starting lineup under manager Carlo Ancelotti. Bruno Guimaraes captained the side and assisted the opening goal after nine minutes.

Vinicius opened the scoring with a left-footed shot past goalkeeper Izwan Mahbud, added a second in the 15th minute following an Endrick layoff, and completed his rapid treble in the 21st minute from an Estevao cross. Endrick extended Brazil's lead further before halftime with a low range effort in the 31st minute, making it 4-0 at the break after earlier goals and efforts were disallowed for offside and fouls.

After the interval, Chelsea winger Estevao added a deflected fifth goal just moments into the second half. Substitute Rayan increased the tally to six in the 65th minute by rounding the goalkeeper, and fellow substitute Allan sealed the 7-0 scoreline in the 74th minute with a low angled shot that deflected off defender Raoul Suhaimi.

stories.title: New York City Mayor Disbands Controversial Police Anti-Terrorism Unit
stories.summary:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced the elimination of a police unit previously criticized for employing heavy-handed methods against demonstrators. Speaking on Monday alongside Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch, Mamdani revealed that the Strategic Response Group, a decade-old anti-terrorism division, will be dissolved to make room for a different, civilian-led framework for managing public demonstrations. During his electoral campaign last year, the mayor had pledged to dismantle the unit, which faced legal scrutiny for mass arrests and the deployment of armed officers in riot gear using pepper spray.

To replace parts of the disbanded organization, the city is establishing an unarmed civilian group named the Community Dialogue and De-escalation Division, which will lack arrest powers. Additionally, a new internal branch called the Patrol Support Division will take over policing protests. The Strategic Response Group originally faced formal condemnation following a 2023 legal agreement resulting from a lawsuit brought by the New York Civil Liberties Union, Attorney General Letitia James, and additional parties regarding excessive force deployed against journalists, legal observers, and protesters during 2020 demonstrations against police violence.

Commissioner Tisch explained that the approximately 500 officers currently assigned to the disbanded unit will be reassigned across the department before the upcoming spring, with certain personnel moving into the existing Counterterrorism Bureau. While Tisch noted that overall crowd control response protocols would remain unchanged, the mayor's office did not clarify whether former unit members would staff the newly formed Patrol Support Division or detail how the new division's operational style would differ.

Civil rights organizations cautiously greeted the dismantling while expressing apprehension that the newly introduced Patrol Support Division might simply function as a reconfigured version of the old unit. The Legal Aid Society praised the termination of the controversial group while emphasizing the necessity of strict oversight, and the New York Civil Liberties Union stated it would closely monitor compliance with the 2023 settlement. Conversely, police unions condemned the policy shift, with Police Benevolent Association President Patrick Hendry arguing that the decision compromises the safety of both officers and residents during disruptive public demonstrations.

stories.title: Pakistan and Sri Lanka Penalized for Slow Over-Rates in Test
stories.summary:
Pakistan and Sri Lanka received severe sanctions for maintaining slow over-rates during the drawn first Test match of their ICC World Test Championship series held in Rawalpindi. Match referee Dean Cosker enforced the penalties after finding Pakistan five overs short and Sri Lanka 15 overs behind the required rate once time allowances were applied. Under the ICC Code of Conduct, players face fines of five percent of their match fees for every short over, capped at 50 percent. Consequently, Pakistan captains and players incurred a 25 percent fine, while Sri Lanka received the maximum 50 percent penalty after both captains, Babar Azam and Kusal Mendis, pleaded guilty to the charges brought by on-field umpires Adrian Holdstock and Rod Tucker alongside third and fourth umpires.

The disciplinary actions further damaged both nations' positions within the 2025-27 WTC standings. Pakistan dropped from nine points to four points, lowering their points percentage to approximately 3.33 percent. Meanwhile, Sri Lanka fell from 28 points down to roughly 15.48 percent, pushing them into eighth place in the nine-team table. This latest sanction compounds ongoing over-rate troubles for Pakistan in the current championship cycle, following a previous 19-point deduction that included an 11-point penalty after their September match against England at Edgbaston. Repeated infractions have heavily undermined Pakistan's campaign, leaving them with minimal chances of reaching the WTC final.

The two-match series continued with the second Test starting on Tuesday in Rawalpindi, offering both squads a chance to rebuild their standings. However, the point deductions from the opening encounter will persist as a permanent setback throughout the remainder of the tournament cycle.

stories.title: Amazon Pledges $7 Billion for Renewable Energy Projects in India
stories.summary:
United States e-commerce giant Amazon announced a $7 billion commitment toward renewable energy projects in India by the year 2030. The initiative aims to expand the company's clean energy presence in one of its primary global growth markets, building upon an already contracted $4 billion investment in Indian renewable power.

The announcement coincides with India's broader national effort to scale up renewable energy and grid infrastructure, targeting 500 gigawatts of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030. Alongside this funding pledge, the retailer unveiled four new solar and wind ventures boasting a combined capacity of 934 megawatts.

These newly introduced green energy projects will be developed across the states of Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan. The initiatives are being undertaken by Indian firms Waaree, Renew, and Sunsure.

stories.title: Indian State Refiners Award 2027 US LPG Tender to Four Suppliers
stories.summary:
A group of India's state-run oil companies jointly awarded a major tender to import approximately 2.75 million metric tons of US liquefied petroleum gas throughout 2027. The participating firms—Indian Oil Corp, Bharat Petroleum Corp, and Hindustan Petroleum Corp—initially floated the tender in September to secure four very large gas carrier cargoes per month on a delivered basis and one cargo monthly on a free-on-board basis.

Under the finalized agreements, Saudi Aramco and Chevron will each supply one delivered cargo per month, TotalEnergies Trading SA will provide two delivered cargoes monthly, and trading firm Vitol will supply one free-on-board cargo each month. A typical very large gas carrier transports about 46,000 tons of LPG, which consists of a propane and butane mixture.

India first began purchasing US LPG this year via annual contracts to offset declining supplies from the Middle East while encouraging households to adopt piped gas. In 2025, the Middle East accounted for roughly 90 percent of India's 21.85 million metric tons of LPG imports. By sourcing up to a quarter of its 2027 LPG from the US, India aims to address trade surplus imbalances with Washington, fulfilling a priority for President Donald Trump as New Delhi pursues a long-delayed bilateral trade pact.

stories.title: Trump Meets Quad Allies in Manila Ahead of China and Russia Talks
stories.summary:
US President Donald Trump met with regional allies India, Japan, and Australia in Manila for a Quad meeting during his three-day Asian tour. Speaking at the Solaire hotel in Paranaque, Metro Manila, Trump emphasized cooperation among the four democracies.

The discussions touched on geopolitical tensions, with the Quad issuing a statement raising concerns over economic coercion and export restrictions. Although no specific country was named, the concerns followed trade restrictions between nations such as Japan and China over critical minerals. The leaders also outlined plans for joint military exercises and artificial intelligence development.

Following the Quad gathering, Trump participated in a US-ASEAN Special Summit and is scheduled to meet Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. Protesters gathered in Manila during the visit, expressing various grievances. Meanwhile, Thailand and the US signed a joint trade statement concerning tariff eliminations.

Trump will next travel to Shenzhen for the APEC forum, where he is anticipated to hold trilateral meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian counterparts. The diplomatic engagements occur amid ongoing trade-war truce discussions and recent US curbs on advanced chip access.

stories.title: Iranian Foreign Minister Meets Pakistan Army Chief in Rawalpindi
stories.summary:
An Iranian high-level delegation led by Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met with Pakistan's Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces, Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, in Rawalpindi on Tuesday. The meeting was arranged to discuss mutual interests, regional security, geopolitical shifts, and strategies to tackle common security challenges.

During the discussions, Field Marshal Munir emphasized that sustained communication, mutual trust, and close cooperation between the two nations are vital for regional peace and stability. In response, Foreign Minister Araghchi commended Pakistan for playing a constructive role in regional stability and expressed Tehran's eagerness to deepen bilateral ties.

Araghchi's visit to Islamabad coincided with his attendance at the Economic Cooperation Organisation meeting, where he advocated for enhanced regional collaboration focused on energy, transport, and trade. He also criticized the United States and Israel for actions against Iran, while reiterating Tehran's adherence to international law and its readiness for diplomatic solutions.

This diplomatic engagement highlights ongoing regional dialogues aimed at fostering security cooperation. By addressing joint challenges and promoting bilateral relations, both Pakistan and Iran continue to work toward mitigating tensions and encouraging peaceful diplomatic engagement across South and Central Asia.

stories.title: Autopsy Finds Severe Injuries on Teen Domestic Worker in Islamabad
stories.summary:
An autopsy report for a 13-year-old domestic worker found dead at the official residence of a senior Federal Investigation Agency official revealed she suffered numerous physical assaults. Identified as Fatima Asghar, the victim allegedly died from repeated violence that caused severe injuries, inflammation, thromboembolism, and subsequent cardiopulmonary arrest. Investigators noted that all documented injuries occurred prior to her death and were severe enough to prove fatal in the ordinary course of life. The examination recorded 20 distinct injuries, including skull swelling, blood clots, old and unhealed burn marks, scars, and extensive bruising across her head, limbs, and torso.

Police arrested the suspects on Sunday after registering a first information report under Section 302 of the Pakistan Penal Code at the Shams Colony police station. The accused individuals include the FIA official's dual-national wife and a Qari who served as an employee at the residence. According to the victim's father, who resides in Rahim Yar Khan, his daughter was a seminary student living with close relatives at a police lines headquarters and had been working at the official's home for roughly two years.

The tragedy drew a public reaction from First Lady Bibi Asifa Bhutto Zardari, who expressed deep sorrow and stressed that Islamabad's four-year-old child employment law strictly forbids hiring children of Fatima's age. She called for a transparent, impartial investigation to ensure those responsible face justice and urged stronger societal efforts to protect vulnerable domestic child workers from abuse.

stories.title: جے شاہ دوبارہ آئی سی سی چیئرمین منتخب، ملے جلے ردعمل کا اظہار
stories.summary:
انٹرنیشنل کرکٹ کونسل (آئی سی سی) کے بورڈ نے بالی میں منعقدہ اجلاس کے دوران جے شاہ کو بلا مقابلہ دوسری مدت کے لیے ادارے کا چیئرمین دوبارہ مقرر کرنے کا اعلان کر دیا ہے۔ جے شاہ کے اس انتخاب کے موقع پر ان کے مقابلے میں کوئی دوسرا امیدوار میدان میں نہیں تھا۔ اس تقرری پر جہاں مختلف حلقوں کی جانب سے مبارکبادیں پیش کی گئیں، وہیں دنیا بھر میں اس پر سوالات اور تنقید کا سلسلہ بھی شروع ہو گیا۔

تقرری کے بعد اپنے بیان میں جے شاہ نے بورڈ کے ڈائریکٹرز کا شکریہ ادا کیا اور کہا کہ وہ 2027 کے ون ڈے ورلڈ کپ اور 2028 کے لاس انجلس اولمپکس میں کرکٹ کی واپسی جیسے اہم مراحل میں عالمی کرکٹ کے مفاد کے لیے کام جاری رکھیں گے۔ تاہم، سوشل میڈیا پر ان کے انتخاب پر اقربا پروری کے الزامات بھی لگائے گئے، اور کچھ ناقدین نے بغیر کسی انتخابی مقابلے کے اس طرح کے طاقتور عہدے پر تقرری کو شفافیت کے منافی قرار دیا۔

بالی ووڈ کے مشہور اداکار شاہ رخ خان نے بھی سوشل میڈیا پر جے شاہ کو مبارکباد دی جس پر صارفین کی جانب سے ملے جلے تبصرے سامنے آئے۔ یاد رہے کہ جے شاہ نے اس سے قبل اگست 2024 میں گریگ بارکلے کی جگہ پہلی بار یہ عہدہ سنبھالا تھا، اور اب وہ ایک بار پھر عالمی کرکٹ کی باگ ڈور سنبھال رہے ہیں۔

stories.title: Ukrainian Drones and Missiles Cripple Kerch Bridge Ahead of Summit
stories.summary:
Ukrainian forces launched a major strike on Tuesday, destroying the central road section of the 19-kilometre bridge connecting Russia and Crimea. Verified footage showed the main road arch collapsing into the Kerch Strait, leaving a significant gap and halting road traffic.

The attack occurred two days before Russian President Vladimir Putin is scheduled to meet US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen. Russian-installed governor Sergei Aksyonov reported two fatalities, while officials noted that rail traffic partially resumed. Analysts suggested that repairs will face severe hurdles due to ongoing military hostilities.

The bridge strike coincided with what Russian state media described as Ukraine's largest drone attack yet, involving hundreds of drones targeting multiple regions, including energy and refinery infrastructure in Bashkortostan and the Moscow area. In response, Russian strikes hit Ukrainian energy infrastructure, the capital city of Kyiv, and transport facilities.

The military escalation follows recent US-brokered peace talks in Abu Dhabi that yielded prisoner exchanges but no broader territorial breakthroughs. Both nations continue a grinding war of attrition, targeting strategic assets despite ongoing diplomatic efforts.

stories.title: Bilawal Defends Parliamentary Opposition and Urges Governance Reform in Speech
stories.summary:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari stated on Tuesday that Pakistan's administrative framework was engineered to fail rather than collapse spontaneously. Addressing an audience at the Karachi Press Club, Bilawal responded to recent government debates initiated by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi regarding a system reset and the creation of new administrative units.

Bilawal acknowledged that a reset is necessary to tackle public hardships such as poverty, unemployment, and inflation, but insisted it must be led by political actors. He admitted personal shortcomings in governance and emphasized the urgent need to rebuild lost trust and legitimacy across state institutions.

During his address, Bilawal also defended Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman amid rising tensions with the government. He criticized attempts to question the patriotism of opposition members, labeling it an injustice to parliament and the country.

The remarks come amid broader political friction and debates concerning the role of the opposition in parliament. Bilawal maintained that opposition parties play a vital patriotic role and have every right to critique government policies.

stories.title: Jurgen Klopp Praises Germany After 5-0 Nations League Win Over Netherlands
stories.summary:
Germany coach Jurgen Klopp expressed strong optimism for his team's future following a 5-0 victory against the Netherlands in Berlin on Monday. The dominant win propelled the four-time champions from third place to the top of their group, securing a spot in the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals.

Klopp, who took over as Germany manager in the summer after their early World Cup elimination, praised the quality and character of his squad. Florian Wirtz scored two goals, while Derry Scherhant, Nico Schlotterbeck, and Brajan Gruda also added to the tally in a match where the Dutch side suffered their first defeat of the tournament.

The victory arrived 150 days after Germany's World Cup exit against Paraguay. Klopp highlighted the integration of talented young players into the squad alongside established stars, creating renewed public confidence in the national team.

Germany will discover their quarter-final opponent during the draw in Switzerland on Friday, with potential matchups including world champions Spain, Portugal, or Belgium. Klopp noted that he is eagerly anticipating the upcoming fixtures against tough competition.

stories.title: South Africa Trails Bangladesh as Bavuma Retires Hurt in Test
stories.summary:
South Africa reached 386 for seven at lunch on the third day of the first Test against Bangladesh at The Wanderers on Tuesday, trailing the visiting side's total of 400 all out by 14 runs. The pitch at the venue continues to offer favorable conditions for batting as the home team looks to establish a lead during the afternoon session.

Captain Temba Bavuma was forced to retire hurt after scoring 49 runs following lingering calf issues and a subsequent leg injury. Before his departure, Bavuma and Ryan Rickelton formed a 79-run partnership for the fifth wicket. Rickelton remained unbeaten on 56 at the interval and was set to resume play alongside Kagiso Rabada, who had five runs.

Bangladesh seamers made key breakthroughs during the session with the new ball. Taskin Ahmed finished with figures of 2 for 88 by dismissing Wiaan Mulder for a duck and Marco Jansen for eight, with wicketkeeper Litton Das catching both. Despite struggling with a sore elbow, Hasan Mahmud claimed 4 for 72 by removing Simon Harmer for one just before lunch, also caught by Das.

Earlier in the match, South Africa's opening batter Marques Ackerman recorded a career-best 157 runs off 164 deliveries, while number three batsman Zubayr Hamza contributed 83 runs upon returning to the lineup. Bavuma remains eligible to return and bat later in the innings if necessary.

stories.title: Pakistan Government Cuts Petrol Price by Rs3 While Keeping Diesel Unchanged
stories.summary:
The federal government of Pakistan announced a reduction in the price of petrol by Rs3 per litre, bringing the new rate to Rs325. Meanwhile, the price of high-speed diesel remained unchanged at Rs358 per litre for November 18, according to a Petroleum Division notification.

This adjustment follows a previous Rs2 reduction for November 17. Earlier measures included oil refineries absorbing costs to maintain lower prices amid global market volatility driven by the US-Israeli conflict with Iran. In July, daily price reviews replaced weekly ones due to supply concerns.

To assist lower-income consumers, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif previously launched a relief scheme offering discounted fuel for motorcycles, rickshaws, and cars under 800cc. Additionally, the government has enforced austerity and conservation measures, requiring commercial venues, markets, and shops to close at specified evening hours.

stories.title: Hailstorm and Rain Cut Short South Africa's Charge Against Bangladesh
stories.summary:
Severe hailstorm and rain halted play on the third day of the opening Test match between South Africa and Bangladesh at the Wanderers. The hosts reached 386-7 after 90 overs, trailing Bangladesh's first-innings total of 400 by 14 runs when bad weather ended the sessions.

South Africa resumed the day at 287-4, building on Marques Ackerman's overnight century of 157. Ryan Rickelton anchored the innings with an unbeaten 56 off 104 balls, while captain Temba Bavuma added 30 runs before retiring hurt with a leg muscle strain on 49. Bangladesh bowlers then claimed crucial late wickets to check the hosts' progress.

Taskin Ahmed dismissed Wiaan Mulder and Marco Jansen, and Hasan Mahmud removed Simon Harmer. Hasan finished as Bangladesh's leading bowler with 4-72, while Taskin picked up two wickets. Kagisa Rabada was not out on five alongside Rickelton when rain stopped play.

Bangladesh had earlier posted 400 runs, driven by centuries from Towhid Hridoy and Litton Das. South Africa's bowling attack in that innings was led by Rabada with five wickets and Dane Paterson with four.

stories.title: Pakistani Rupee Edges Up Slightly Against US Dollar
stories.summary:
The Pakistani rupee recorded a marginal increase against the US dollar in the inter-bank market on Tuesday. At the close of the trading day, the domestic currency finished at 276.56, marking a rise of Re0.01 compared to the previous day when it closed at 276.57.

On the international stage, the US dollar reached a new 19-month high against a basket of peer currencies on Tuesday. This movement was driven by expectations of stricter monetary policy tightening by the US Federal Reserve following recent high inflation figures and hawkish remarks from central bank officials. The greenback also extended a 10-month high against the Australian currency as a worldwide selloff in artificial intelligence stocks affected market sentiment and weakened the risk-sensitive Australian dollar.

Accelerating consumer inflation in the United States last week sparked five consecutive days of gains for the US dollar index, extending into a sixth day on Tuesday to reach 103.66, which is its highest level since April 2, 2025, when President Donald Trump introduced his tariffs. The index tracks the greenback against six major currencies, including the euro, British pound, and Japanese yen. Market participants now view a Federal Reserve interest rate increase at the December meeting as certain, with the CME Group’s FedWatch tool indicating about four percent probability for an oversized half-point hike.

Meanwhile, oil prices declined on Tuesday as anticipated supply surpluses stemming from recovering Middle East exports outweighed worries regarding ongoing tanker attacks and broader geopolitical tensions. Brent crude futures dropped by 78 cents, or 0.8 percent, to $91.66 a barrel by 0430 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate futures fell by 73 cents, or 0.9 percent, to $84.99 a barrel.

stories.title: MS Dhoni Retires From IPL Play to Become Chennai Mentor
stories.summary:
Former India cricket captain MS Dhoni has ended his playing career in the Indian Premier League and transitioned into a mentoring position with the Chennai Super Kings, the franchise announced on Tuesday. The 45-year-old wicketkeeper-batter, who last represented India internationally in 2019, guided Chennai to five tournament titles, establishing the team as one of the most successful in the competition.

Chennai owner Rupa Gurunath praised the player in a statement, noting that his experience and expertise will prove especially valuable as the franchise works to nurture younger athletes during a transition period. Chennai finished eighth in the 10-team standings during a disappointing campaign this year, having last won the championship trophy in 2023.

Throughout his career with the franchise, Dhoni accumulated 5,314 runs, making him Chennai's second-highest run-scorer. He also holds the record for the most appearances for the team with 272 matches played. Widely known as "Captain Cool" for his calm demeanor under pressure, he earned renown for his finishing skills and ability to guide the team through challenging run chases.

On the international stage, Dhoni led India to victory in the 2007 T20 World Cup and the 2011 ODI World Cup. Although he retired from international cricket in 2020, he continued playing in the IPL, though lingering knee issues and declining batting form limited his on-field impact in recent years. Chennai managing director Kasi Viswanathan stated that while fans will miss seeing him wear yellow on the field, the franchise is pleased he will continue guiding the players. The auction for the 2027 IPL season is set for December 16 in Goa.

stories.title: Copper Hits Multi-Month Low as Technology Sector Weakness Pressures Prices
stories.summary:
Copper prices declined to their lowest level in four and a half months on Tuesday. The drop was driven by weakness in technology stocks that sparked concerns regarding artificial intelligence-related investments and dampened risk appetite, while a stronger US dollar and expectations of rising interest rates added further downward pressure.

Benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange decreased by 0.3 percent to $13,211.50 per metric ton by 0955 GMT, after touching $13,144 earlier in the session, marking its lowest price point since July 1. Asian stock markets declined following Washington's announcement that it would implement further restrictions on China's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips from companies like Nvidia, tightening regulations as President Donald Trump traveled to China for discussions with President Xi Jinping.

According to ING commodities strategist Ewa Manthey, the selloff in artificial intelligence shares has raised worries about the demand outlook for copper, given the metal's increasing exposure to investments in data centers and power grids. Despite these pressures, signs of tight prompt supply provided some backing for copper, reflected by an increase in the Yangshan copper premium—an indicator of China's demand for imported metal—and the premium of the LME cash copper contract over the benchmark.

The strengthening US dollar reached a 19-month peak on Tuesday amid expectations of aggressive monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve, making dollar-priced metals more expensive for purchasers using other currencies. Meanwhile, LME aluminum dropped 1.2 percent to $2,967 after hitting a one-month low of $2,965, and the premium of the LME cash contract over the three-month contract reached $278 a ton, the highest level recorded since 1988 due to low stock levels. Other metals saw mixed results, with LME zinc losing 0.6 percent to $3,676, lead remaining stable at $1,875, nickel gaining 0.6 percent to $15,945, and tin rising 0.5 percent to $46,285.

stories.title: Pakistan HEC Announces 61 Chinese Government Scholarships for 2027–28
stories.summary:
The Higher Education Commission (HEC) of Pakistan has officially rolled out the Chinese Government Scholarship Programme for the 2027–28 academic year, opening doors for local scholars to pursue degrees at universities across China. Managed via the Chinese Scholarship Council, a total of 61 slots have been designated for Pakistani applicants seeking higher education opportunities abroad.

The distribution of these funded positions includes 25 undergraduate slots, 21 master's positions, and 15 PhD opportunities. The HEC is acting as the official nominating entity for candidates applying through the designated Type-A framework, requiring all interested parties to utilize its online portal before the cutoff time of 4:00 pm on January 5, 2027.

Authorities have stressed that only records formally updated to a "Submitted" status on the application portal will move forward in the evaluation pipeline. Drafts left unsubmitted will be automatically disqualified from consideration. Candidates opting for Type-B or alternative funding pathways must manage their paperwork and direct correspondence independently without HEC nomination.

Additionally, the China Scholastic Competency Assessment (CSCA) has been declared a mandatory testing prerequisite for anyone targeting undergraduate studies within Chinese institutions. This rule applies universally across all scholarship channels, including Type-A HEC nominees and Type-B applicants alike, prompting officials to urge thorough reviews of all posted guidelines prior to submission.

stories.title: NDMA Issues Severe Drought Alert for Districts in Sindh and Balochistan
stories.summary:
The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), through its National Emergency Operations Centre, has sounded a high alert warning of potential severe drought emergencies spanning multiple regions in Sindh and Balochistan. Officials pointed to prolonged dry spells, below-average rainfall totals, rising temperatures, and shifting monsoon patterns as the primary drivers behind the crisis.

The areas facing the highest threats include parts of the Umerkot, Tharparkar, Mirpurkhas, and Sujawal districts in Sindh, alongside select pockets of Chagai and Washuk in Balochistan. Local weather stations have recorded temperatures running one to three degrees Celsius higher than typical seasonal averages across the endangered zones in Sindh, worsening ecological stress.

This unfolding environmental strain has severely disrupted regional agricultural operations and crop yields, sparking deep worries regarding household and regional food security. The National Emergency Operations Centre is maintaining continuous surveillance over the developing situation as ground conditions remain under close watch.

In response to the hazard, the NDMA has instructed relevant administrative bodies to optimize local water supplies and deploy preventative safeguards aimed at shielding vulnerable rural populations and farming communities. Residents have simultaneously been urged to adhere strictly to safety advisories issued by local authorities to safeguard their livestock and harvests.

stories.title: MS Dhoni Concludes Playing Career and Joins Chennai as Mentor
stories.summary:
Mahendra Singh Dhoni has formally concluded his playing career in the Indian Premier League, taking on a new role as team mentor for the Chennai Super Kings. The 45-year-old athlete, widely celebrated as a pivotal figure in the franchise's history, previously stepped away from international cricket back in the year 2020.

During his illustrious tenure on the field, Dhoni captained the Chennai squad to a remarkable five Indian Premier League trophies alongside two Champions League Twenty20 titles. Hailing from Ranchi, he maintained a profound connection with supporters in Chennai, where fans frequently packed stadiums simply to catch a glimpse of the leader affectionately known locally as "Thala."

Although recent seasons saw a decline in his batting output down the order, large crowds continued to fill the stands to watch him play. However, a persistent calf strain forced him to sit out the entirety of the most recent season, ultimately bringing his active playing days to a close. Except for two seasons with the Rising Pune Super Giant during Chennai's two-year suspension over a corruption scandal, Dhoni remained the face of the franchise from his arrival in 2008 onward.

Team owner N. Srinivasan praised Dhoni as an integral part of the franchise's identity, noting that selecting him in the 2008 draft was the best decision in the club's history. Managing director K.S. Viswanathan also expressed relief that Dhoni will remain onboard to counsel younger players, ensuring his leadership will continue to shape the team's trajectory for years to come.

stories.title: Over 8,000 Hoax Bomb Threats Disrupt European Schools and Airports
stories.summary:
More than 8,000 bomb hoaxes targeted businesses and institutions across Europe over the span of a month, according to disclosures by European officials, media reports, and cybersecurity firms like Proofpoint and Mimecast. The campaign primarily affected schools in the United Kingdom, Ireland, and Italy, while also disrupting airlines, airports, media organizations, and charities. Notable incidents included threats sent to approximately 300 schools in Northern Ireland and Scotland on October 19 with the subject line "Death is near," prompting evacuations and room searches.

The wave of disruptions continued into November, forcing dozens of flight diversions and cancellations. Flight tracking specialists AirNav Radar reported that over 50 flights across roughly 15 airlines received hoax threats between November 2 and November 6. Media outlets, such as France's TF1, Bulgaria's Nova, and Irish broadcaster RTE, were also targeted, briefly knocking some programs off the air. A significantly larger wave occurred on November 11, when about 6,300 Italian schools, along with roughly 1,000 schools in Scotland and 300 each in Northern Ireland and Ireland, received threats purportedly originating from a group called "Misoginistan" or "Male State."

European officials, including French interior minister Laurent Nuñez, have stated they suspect foreign interference, specifically pointing to Russia or other potential countries, while Europol works to determine the origin of the threats. Cybersecurity experts noted similarities in the wording and distribution methods, suggesting the use of a shared target list. School principals and authorities emphasized that despite appearing implausible or reckless, the threats had to be treated with extreme seriousness due to safety concerns.

The mass-distributed emails were sent from at least four hijacked email accounts, including one belonging to a former graduate student at Da-Yeh University in Taiwan. While previous bomb hoaxes in Western government entities had been linked by cybersecurity firms to suspected Russian mercenary hackers known as the DaVinci Group, officials continue extensive inquiries to confirm direct connections. The widespread disruptions have left communities and institutions on high alert as investigations into the source of the campaign persist.

stories.title: Massive Fire Destructs Glass Factory Following Oil Tanker Blast in Karachi
stories.summary:
A large-scale fire erupted at an industrial facility situated in Karachi’s Baldia Town on Tuesday morning, triggered during the replenishment of an underground fuel repository by an oil tanker. Rescue-1122 received initial alerts regarding the incident at approximately 10:36 am, dispatching multiple fire units to the Rasheedabad location as the emergency escalated.

The targeted structure was a two-storey commercial property operated as the Al-Hamad Plastic Factory, which specialized in producing decorative items and windowpanes. According to initial findings detailed by Rescue spokesperson Hassaanul Haseeb Khan, the blaze originated when the oil tanker caught fire and exploded during the fuel transfer, propelling burning oil across the factory grounds and onto surrounding streets and creating widespread panic.

Roughly 70 percent of the raging fire had been successfully contained by teams utilizing 11 fire tenders, which worked to prevent the flames from spreading further across the ground, first, and second floors. While the definitive trigger remains subject to a comprehensive forensic investigation regarding potential human error during refueling, the tanker itself was entirely incinerated in the accident.

Police officials alongside the Site-B police station confirmed that no injuries or fatalities resulted from the emergency. Sindh Rangers units were likewise deployed to the scene to assist rescue crews and regulate local traffic flow, as municipal authorities continue broader safety audits across commercial buildings throughout the city's seven districts.

stories.title: India Defeats Pakistan to Win Record Tenth SAFF Championship Title
stories.summary:
Pakistan's historic bid for a maiden SAFF Championship title ended in heartbreak on Tuesday at the National Stadium in Dhaka, where India secured a 2-1 comeback victory in the final. Late substitute Sandip Mandi scored the winning goal in the 87th minute, extending India's record to ten regional crowns and securing their third consecutive championship. The defeat was particularly cruel for Pakistan, who had dominated much of the match and held the lead through the first half.

Pakistan controlled the opening exchanges and maintained 65 percent possession in the first half compared to India's 35 percent, outshooting their opponents nine to four. Their dominance paid off in first-half stoppage time when Alamghir Ghazi curled a shot into the far corner past goalkeeper Yousuf Butt's efforts, giving Pakistan a 1-0 advantage at the interval. It was Ghazi's second goal of the tournament, with both of his strikes coming against India.

India increased their attacking pressure after the break. Pakistan's hopes suffered a major setback in the 57th minute when midfielder Junaid Shah received a red card following a VAR review for a rough challenge, leaving the Green-shirts with ten men. India capitalized almost immediately when Sohail Ahmed Butt scored his fourth goal of the tournament to equalize in the 58th minute. Despite being a man down, Pakistan maintained a resilient defensive shape.

The resilient defense held until the 87th minute, when Sandip Mandi found the net to put India ahead for the first time in the match. Pakistan pushed for a late equalizer but failed to break through, allowing India to hold on and claim the championship trophy once again.

stories.title: Post-Mortem Reveals Brutal Violence in Islamabad Domestic Worker's Death
stories.summary:
The post-mortem report of 13-year-old domestic worker Fatima Asghar revealed approximately 20 major wounds and visible marks of physical violence spanning from her head to her toes. Conducted by the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences, the examination documented severe physical trauma, untreated infections resulting in pus and foul odor, blood clots in the heart and kidneys, and burn marks consistent with a heated iron. Fatima was employed at the Islamabad residence of a senior Police Service of Pakistan officer posted in Gujranwala.

The girl's death on November 14 was initially reported as mysterious, and local police allegedly attempted to keep the matter quiet before senior officials intervened and a case was registered at the Shams Colony Police Station. Two suspects, Afshan—a Pakistani-origin Canadian national and wife of the police officer—and Qari Ali, a tutor and Punjab Highway Patrol employee, were arrested and granted a four-day physical remand by an Islamabad district court. During police interrogation, the suspects gave contradictory statements.

Afshan denied ever subjecting the minor to physical violence. However, Qari Ali claimed he beat Fatima on Afshan's instructions, adding that he complied out of fear of losing his job. Following these disclosures, police conducted a surprise raid at the officer's residence within the Police Lines Headquarters, recovering an iron on Afshan's identification and sticks and canes on Ali's identification. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi stated that the police pursued the case despite initial reluctance from the victim's father and are conducting a thorough investigation.

The case has drawn widespread condemnation and calls for justice. First Lady Bibi Asifa Bhutto Zardari expressed deep sorrow over the incident, emphasizing that under Islamabad's four-year-old child employment law, no child of that age could be employed as a domestic worker. She called for a transparent, impartial investigation and strict enforcement of child protection laws to prevent further exploitation and abuse of vulnerable children in domestic settings.

stories.title: بحرین میں دھماکے، پاسدارانِ انقلاب کا امریکی ریڈار نشانہ بنانے کا دعویٰ
stories.summary:
بحرین کے دارالحکومت منامہ میں دھماکوں کی آوازیں سنی گئی ہیں جبکہ بحرین کے سرکاری ٹی وی نے ایران کی جانب سے کیے جانے والے حملے روکنے کا دعویٰ کیا ہے۔ اس سے قبل ایرانی پاسدارانِ انقلاب نے بحرین کے جزیرے پر واقع شیخ عیسیٰ اڈے میں امریکی افواج کے ایک ریڈار سسٹم کو نشانہ بنانے کا دعویٰ کیا تھا۔ بحرین کی وزارتِ داخلہ نے ممکنہ خطرے کے پیشِ نظر شہریوں کے لیے انتباہ جاری کرتے ہوئے محفوظ مقامات پر جانے کی ہدایت کی ہے۔

دوسری جانب جاپان، جنوبی کوریا اور تائیوان کی جانب سے فضائی حدود اور ڈیفنس زون میں روسی طیاروں کی موجودگی پر ردِعمل سامنے آیا ہے۔ جاپان نے دو مشتبہ روسی طیاروں کی جانب سے فضائی حدود کی خلافورزی پر سخت احتجاج ریکارڈ کرایا اور لڑاکا طیارے روانہ کیے۔ یہ واقعات چین میں ہونے والے ایپیک سربراہی اجلاس سے قبل پیش آئے ہیں۔ ادھر یمن میں حوثیوں کے مطابق صنعا پر فضائی حملے میں نو افراد زخمی ہوئے جبکہ پاکستان کے زیرِ انتظام کشمیر کے علاقے راولاکوٹ میں فائرنگ سے پاکستان رینجرز کے ڈپٹی سپرنٹنڈنٹ برکت ہلاک ہو گئے۔

راولپنڈی میں ایرانی وزیر خارجہ عباس عراقچی نے فیلڈ مارشل عاصم منیر سے ملاقات کی جس میں علاقائی سکیورٹی اور باہمی دلچسپی کے امور پر تبادلہ خیال کیا گیا۔ دریں اثنا ایرانی فوج کے ترجمان امیر اکرم نیا نے کہا ہے کہ آبنائے ہرمز اس وقت کھولی جائے گی جب امریکہ ایران کی سات شرائط تسلیم کر لے گا۔ ایرانی پارلیمان کے سپیکر محمد باقر قالیباف نے بھی خبردار کیا ہے کہ اگر ایران کے آبی بنیادی ڈھانچے کو نشانہ بنایا گیا تو تہران بھرپور جوابی کارروائی کرے گا۔

stories.title: Asian Buddhist Leaders Explore Pakistan's Ancient Gandhara Heritage
stories.summary:
An international delegation of Buddhist monks and religious scholars from eight Asian countries visited the Islamabad Museum and the historic Shah Allah Ditta Caves on Tuesday. The high-profile visit was part of the three-day Gandhara Strategic Dialogue 2026, held under the theme "Towards a Shared Future" to promote international cooperation for the preservation and global recognition of Gandhara's Buddhist heritage. The initiative is led by Imran Shaukat, coordinator to the Prime Minister's Task Force on Gandhara.

The visiting delegation included senior religious figures from Thailand, Laos, Vietnam, Japan, Cambodia, Sri Lanka, South Korea, and Bangladesh. At the Islamabad Museum, the monks and scholars viewed an extensive collection of Gandharan antiquities, including Buddha sculptures, relics, and artifacts showcasing the region's historical and spiritual significance. They also experienced an immersive digital presentation detailing the ancient civilization's history.

Following the museum tour, the delegation traveled to the Shah Allah Ditta Caves, an archaeological site linked to the area's Buddhist past. Accompanied by Tanzeela Sabahat, Joint Secretary of the National Heritage and Culture Division, the visitors explored the site to connect with a heritage that remains important to Buddhist communities across Asia. The dialogue sessions cover topics such as faith-based visitor facilitation, conservation, sacred manuscripts, tourism infrastructure, and community participation.

Opening at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and concluding at the Ministry of National Heritage and Culture Division, the dialogue aims to position Gandhara as a shared civilisational legacy. Imran Shaukat stated that the initiative demonstrates Pakistan's commitment to engaging with the international Buddhist community, using Gandhara as a bridge for cultural diplomacy, interfaith understanding, and global cooperation.

stories.title: Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari Claims Pakistan's System Was Engineered to Collapse
stories.summary:
Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari asserted on Tuesday that the country's political structure did not simply fail on its own accord, but was deliberately engineered to collapse. Speaking at the Karachi Press Club during a virtual address to more than 150 district headquarters and cities on the occasion of the 57th PPP Foundation Day, Bilawal shared his remarks amid a wider national conversation concerning a potential system reset.

The PPP leader's statements coincide with his recent political engagements, which included a telephone call with Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-F leader Fazlur Rehman. During that discussion, Bilawal strongly denounced government actions and political vengeance directed against the JUI-F. He has consistently advocated for unity through a political reset, urging Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to foster trust with both political allies and the parliamentary opposition.

The 57th foundation day celebrations drew significant attention as party officials and supporters gathered via video link to observe the milestone. Bilawal's commentary on governance and institutional stability highlights ongoing political tensions in Pakistan, where opposition figures and coalition partners frequently debate the required direction for economic, judicial, and political reforms.

Such discussions regarding institutional integrity remain central to Pakistan's current political climate, as leaders across the spectrum address structural challenges. The debate over a system reset involves diverse perspectives from political parties, judiciary observers, and government officials seeking to navigate the country's complex governance landscape.

stories.title: Bangladesh Garment Workers Clash With Police Over Delayed Wage Talks
stories.summary:
Bangladeshi law enforcement deployed tear gas and stun grenades on Tuesday to disperse thousands of garment workers who clashed in Dhaka and surrounding industrial districts. The unrest erupted following the sudden postponement of a critical wage board meeting, prompting demonstrators to hurl bricks, set fire to vehicles, and barricade the main highway connecting Dhaka to the financial hub of Mymensingh.

Bangladesh, a South Asian nation of 170 million people, operates the world's second-biggest garment export sector behind China, supplying international brands like Levi Strauss and Fruit of the Loom. The industry generates $38 billion in annual revenues and provides jobs for more than four million citizens. However, escalating worker discontent that began in October has threatened production, with approximately 500 out of 4,500 factories currently shut down.

Employees are demanding a monthly minimum wage of 30,000 taka, equivalent to $240, which represents a 140 percent increase from the current baseline of 12,500 taka. Workers report struggling to manage surging expenses related to food, housing, healthcare, and transport. Compounding the friction is a labor law provision allowing owners to suspend operations and withhold wages during disruptions under a "no work, no pay" policy.

The government established a wage board earlier in the month to negotiate pay adjustments, with a new minimum wage scheduled for announcement in December to take effect in January. Following Monday's meeting delay—attributed to an ailing workers' representative—the next session was rescheduled for November 23. In response to Tuesday's violence, the Border Guard Bangladesh deployed hundreds of personnel equipped with drones and body cameras across industrial zones to monitor security as the sector faces its busiest export period leading up to Christmas.

stories.title: SMEDA Launches Rs5 Million Matching Grants for Textile SMEs
stories.summary:
The Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority, operating under the Ministry of Industries and Production, has officially invited applications from small and medium enterprises for matching grants. The initiative is designed to establish industrial stitching units across Pakistan under the second phase of the "1000 Industrial Stitching Units" programme.

This federal program aims to bolster Pakistan's apparel and textile sector, stimulate export-driven growth, and assist SMEs in expanding their production capacities to reach international markets. Under the financing structure, the government provides a 60 to 40 matching grant, covering 60 percent of eligible project costs while the participating SME contributes the remaining 40 percent. The maximum grant available is capped at Rs. 5 million or 60 percent of machinery expenses, whichever amount is lower.

Eligibility extends to four distinct categories of enterprises: established exporters currently dealing in textile exports, prospective exporters intending to expand export-focused operations, startups seeking to enter the textile export market, and export-linked SMEs indirectly involved through partnerships or orders from larger exporters. Targeted industries encompass readymade garments, fashion apparel, knitwear and hosiery, home textiles, denim and leather garments, canvas, gloves, sports apparel, and traditional textiles.

Interested business owners can access application forms via the official SMEDA website or submit inquiries through designated electronic mail channels. The final deadline for all enterprise application submissions is set for November 30, 2026.

stories.title: Federal Constitutional Court Rebukes LDA Over Litigation Against Hero's Family
stories.summary:
The Federal Constitutional Court of Pakistan has sharply criticized the Lahore Development Authority for continuously targeting the family of Pilot Officer Rashid Minhas Shaheed, a recipient of the prestigious Nishan-i-Haider military award. Authored by Justice Ali Baqar Najafi, the judgment directed the municipal authority to cease squandering public funds and institutional resources on vexatious and frivolous litigation against private individuals.

The legal dispute centered on a 14-marla plot located in Gulberg-III, Lahore, involving a consent decree initially granted in May 2005 in favor of Farooq Minhas, the martyred pilot officer's brother. Although the Lahore Development Authority repeatedly raised objections during subsequent execution proceedings—arguing that the land was evacuee property acquired by its predecessor—three successive legal forums, including the executing court, revisional court, and Lahore High Court, consistently dismissed the authority's claims.

A three-member FCC bench, presided over by Justice Najafi alongside Justice Rozi Khan Barrech and Justice Syed Arshad Hussain Shah, evaluated the LDA director general's appeal against a March 2018 high court ruling. The bench noted that previous judicial decisions had already attained finality and that the initial consent decree was issued with the LDA's own lack of objection. Furthermore, the Supreme Court had previously dismissed a similar petition from the authority, confirming it held no ownership rights over the land.

Concluding the proceedings, the Federal Constitutional Court officially dismissed the LDA's appeal for lacking merit and denied leave to appeal. Instead of imposing financial costs, the bench explicitly ordered the LDA director general to ensure that no further public money is depleted on unnecessary legal battles against citizens.

stories.title: کیا حجاب یا ہیلمٹ کے استعمال سے بال جھڑنے لگتے ہیں؟
stories.summary:
برطانوی نیشنل ہیلتھ سروس (این ایچ ایس) کے مطابق روزانہ 50 سے 100 بال جھڑنا معمول کی بات ہے، لیکن اس سے زیادہ ہونے یا نئے بال نہ اُگنے کی کیفیت کو 'ایلوپیشیا' کہا جاتا ہے۔ دنیا بھر میں 14 کروڑ سے زائد افراد مکمل یا جزوی گنج پن کا شکار ہیں۔ بالوں کا جھڑنا بیماری، ہارمونز کی تبدیلی، غذائی اجزا کی کمی، ذہنی دباؤ یا موروثی وجوہات کی بنا پر ہو سکتا ہے۔ مردوں اور خواتین میں بال جھڑنے کے انداز مختلف ہوتے ہیں۔

ڈاکٹر شائلہ حق کے مطابق جسم میں آئرن، وٹامن ڈی، زنک اور پروٹین کی کمی بالوں کو کمزور کرتی ہے۔ گرم اور مرطوب موسم میں طویل وقت تک ہیلمٹ پہننے یا حجاب رکھنے سے پسینہ جمع ہوتا ہے، جس سے فنگس یا بیکٹیریا کا انفیکشن ہو سکتا ہے۔ ماہرین کا کہنا ہے کہ صرف حجاب یا ہیلمٹ پہننے سے بال نہیں جھڑتے، بلکہ سخت باندھنے سے بالوں کی جڑوں پر دباؤ پڑتا ہے جسے 'ٹریکشن ایلوپیشیا' کہتے ہیں۔ گیلے بالوں کے ساتھ ہیلمٹ پہننے سے بھی بال ٹوٹنے کا خطرہ بڑھ جاتا ہے۔

ماہرین مشورہ دیتے ہیں کہ ہیلمٹ کے پیڈ کو صاف رکھا جائے، پسینے سے بھیگا ہیلمٹ طویل وقت تک نہ پہنا جائے اور بال مکمل خشک ہونے کے بعد ہی ہیلمٹ استعمال کیا جائے۔ اسی طرح حجاب کو بھی قدرے ڈھیلا باندھنا چاہیے تاکہ ہوا کی آمدورفت بحال رہے۔ بال جھڑنے کی اصل وجہ معلوم کر کے بروقت علاج اور مناسب دیکھ بھال سے اس مسئلے کو کم کیا جا سکتا ہے۔

stories.title: Pakistan and Turkmenistan to Advance TAPI Pipeline and Bilateral Ties
stories.summary:
Pakistan and Turkmenistan held the sixth session of their Joint Intergovernmental Commission in Islamabad on Tuesday, focusing heavily on the Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India gas pipeline project. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar hosted a delegation led by Turkmenistan's Foreign Minister Rashid Meredov for the talks, which also preceded the 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation Council of Ministers.

During a joint press briefing, Meredov announced that both nations agreed to convene a meeting of the steering committee for the 1,800-kilometre pipeline. The project is designed to transport 33 billion cubic metres of natural gas annually from Turkmenistan's Galkynysh gas field to Fazilka in India, traversing Herat and Kandahar in Afghanistan as well as Quetta and Multan in Pakistan. The initiative involves a free flow phase costing between $5 billion and $6 billion alongside at least $1.9 billion for compressor stations.

The two sides signed the protocol for the JIC session, a programme of cooperation for their foreign ministries covering 2026 to 2030, and a tourism memorandum. Discussions additionally covered a bilateral transit trade framework, a proposed electricity transmission project with a fibre optic link, and potential railway connectivity utilizing Chabahar and Gwadar ports.

Progress on the pipeline had previously faced repeated delays due to security concerns within Afghanistan. The latest engagements aim to sustain regular diplomatic interaction and boost regional connectivity, with Meredov noting that Turkmenistan intends to arrange a state visit to Islamabad next year.

stories.title: Pakistan Pace Bowlers Dismiss Sri Lanka for 98 in Rawalpindi Test
stories.summary:
Pakistan's pace attack delivered a dominant performance on Tuesday, bowling out Sri Lanka for just 98 runs on the opening day of the second Test at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium. After winning the toss and choosing to field, the home team exploited favorable movement and pace, dismantling the visiting batting lineup in 35.3 overs.

Sri Lanka's innings struggled from the beginning, plunging to 36-5 before Kusal Mendis and Sonal Dinusha formed a 49-run partnership for the sixth wicket. Kusal led the scoring with 32 runs, while Dinusha added 21. However, once that partnership ended, the remaining four wickets fell quickly for just 13 runs, sealing a rapid collapse for the visitors.

Mohammad Abbas, debutant Razaullah, and Aamer Jamal each claimed three wickets, while Saqib Khan picked up one to complete the four-pronged bowling effort. Abbas maintained tight accuracy, while Razaullah and Jamal applied consistent aggression. Their combined efforts left the Sri Lankan lower order with virtually no answers.

In response, Pakistan's opening batters, Tayyab Arif and Azan Awais, safely navigated a testing spell from Sri Lanka's new-ball bowlers. By the tea interval, Pakistan reached 58 without loss, trailing by 40 runs. Tayyab remained unbeaten on 34 alongside Azan on 18, putting the home side in a commanding position.

stories.title: Indian Equities Rise to Highest Level Since February Amid Weakness in Asia
stories.summary:
India's main stock indexes achieved their highest closing levels since late February on Tuesday, successfully defying a broader downturn across other Asian markets. The Nifty 50 advanced 0.38 percent to reach 25,387.40, while the Sensex increased by 0.52 percent to settle at 82,532.19. This ongoing market momentum has been sustained by significant foreign portfolio investor inflows, which have reached a record $9.53 billion during the month, pushing the indexes up by roughly 10.1 percent and 10.8 percent respectively.

In contrast, other Asian regional markets tracked Wall Street lower. This regional decline was primarily driven by weakness within technology stocks after the United States escalated measures to restrict China's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips, alongside general market caution ahead of upcoming earnings reports from Nvidia. Despite the broader regional retreat, eleven out of the sixteen major domestic sectors in India advanced, with banking and private banking shares climbing 1.1 percent and 0.9 percent to hit record highs.

Lower crude oil prices also provided strong support to domestic equities, as Brent crude hovered near $93 a barrel amid expectations of a supply surplus driven by recovering Middle East exports. The declining oil market has notably improved fuel marketing margins for oil marketing companies like BPCL, HPCL, and Indian Oil, while simultaneously easing raw material input cost pressures for various tyre and paint manufacturers.

Individual stock movements showed mixed results during the session, highlighted by Senco Gold jumping 3.5 percent following a 26 percent year-on-year increase in net sales value over the festive period. Conversely, brokerage equities such as Billionbrains and Angel One retreated from earlier gains after news reports indicated that India's financial markets regulator is actively considering new restrictions on leveraged stock purchases in response to record levels of margin-funded trading.

stories.title: Pakistan Records Current Account Surplus of $39 Million in October 2026
stories.summary:
Pakistan achieved a current account surplus of $39 million in October 2026, according to official financial data published by the State Bank of Pakistan on Tuesday. This positive financial result contrasts with a revised current account deficit of $371 million recorded in September 2026 and a deficit of $307 million observed during October of the previous year.

The unexpected monthly surplus was primarily driven by a substantial growth in overseas workers' remittances. According to Sana Tawfik, Head of Research at Arif Habib Limited, the surplus was supported by a 14 percent year-on-year increase in remittances, which reached $3.9 billion, alongside a 10 percent expansion in goods exports.

While robust remittance inflows provided a vital cushion, import demand continued to exert economic pressure, resulting in a trade deficit that widened by 9 percent year-on-year to $3.2 billion. Total goods and services exports for October 2026 reached $3.87 billion, marking a nearly 12 percent increase compared to $3.46 billion in the same period last year. Total imports concurrently rose by over 10 percent to reach $7.08 billion.

Looking ahead, analysts anticipate that the current account deficit will remain manageable throughout fiscal year 2027, staying within the State Bank of Pakistan's projected target range of zero to one percent of gross domestic product. For the first four months of fiscal year 2027, the cumulative current account deficit stands at $850 million, showing an improvement compared to the deficit of $1,062 million recorded during the corresponding period of the prior year.

stories.title: PTI Leaders Arrested Under MPO Following Peshawar High Court Bail Grant
stories.summary:
Police arrested Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf leaders Taimur Saleem Jhagra and Kamran Bangash on Tuesday under the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance. The arrests occurred following a series of events that began when an anti-terrorism court dismissed their bail applications alongside party member Irfan Saleem regarding the May 9, 2023, Radio Pakistan attack case.

The defence argued during the anti-terrorism court hearing that the case was brought forward nearly three years after the incident using video footage that merely showed the politicians present at a protest. Conversely, the prosecution maintained that the suspects incited unrest and that their identities were verified by NADRA and the Punjab Forensic Science Agency. After the anti-terrorism court rejected their pre-arrest bail, police attempted to detain the politicians at the district courts, leading to brief detentions and a security breach as lawyers intervened and broke gates to reach the Peshawar High Court.

Chief Justice SM Attique Shah of the Peshawar High Court subsequently granted the three petitioners interim pre-arrest bail against surety bonds of one million rupees each and scheduled the next hearing for November 23. The court directed the applicants to cooperate with the investigation officer.

Despite the high court's protective order, Peshawar police arrested Jhagra and Bangash under separate detention warrants issued under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance. The politicians maintained they had no connection to the events, while PTI central secretary information Waqas Akram strongly condemned the detentions as an assault on constitutional rights and judicial authority.

stories.title: Pakistan and UK Army Chiefs Hold High-Level Talks on Defense Cooperation
stories.summary:
A senior military delegation from the United Kingdom, headed by Chief of the General Staff General Sir Roly Walker, visited General Headquarters in Rawalpindi on Tuesday. Upon arrival at the military headquarters, the visiting British general was formally welcomed and received a Guard of Honour presented by a smartly turned-out contingent of the Pakistan Army.

The delegation held comprehensive discussions with Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, who serves as the Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces. During the formal meeting, both military leaders addressed matters of mutual interest, evaluated the prevailing regional security environment, and explored concrete avenues for enhancing bilateral defense and security cooperation.

According to the Inter-Services Public Relations, both sides expressed mutual satisfaction regarding the longstanding and cordial diplomatic ties between Pakistan and the United Kingdom. They reaffirmed a shared commitment to further strengthening bilateral military-to-military relations and expanding cooperation across defense sectors.

Field Marshal Asim Munir specifically emphasized Pakistan's dedication to deepening defense ties with the United Kingdom. In response, General Sir Roly Walker praised the high level of professionalism and operational preparedness demonstrated by the Pakistan Armed Forces, while also acknowledging their ongoing contributions toward maintaining regional peace and stability.

stories.title: Pakistan and United Kingdom Draft Agreement to Boost Mineral Investment
stories.summary:
Pakistan and the United Kingdom are currently preparing a bilateral cooperation agreement designed to encourage investment and strengthen collaboration within the critical minerals sector. According to announcements from the British High Commission, a draft Memorandum of Understanding has been formulated between the Geological Survey of Pakistan and the British Geological Survey.

The proposed framework aims to enhance joint institutional cooperation across multiple technical areas, including geological mapping, scientific research, and systematic data sharing. Under this initiative, both organizations will work closely together to support the sustainable development of mineral resources, improve overall transparency, and promote environmental sustainability within the mining industry.

As part of ongoing preparatory efforts, staff members from the Geological Survey of Pakistan recently completed a comprehensive 16-week technical training program. Pakistani experts received specialized instruction in digital geological surveys, geochemical sampling, geographic information systems, and spectral remote sensing.

Speaking at the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum, British High Commissioner Jane Marriott noted that the mining sector presently contributes less than two percent to the country's Gross Domestic Product. She stressed that reliable geological data is vital to attracting international investment and building investor confidence, adding that the United Kingdom is actively supporting Pakistan's minerals sector through the REMIT program. Pakistan holds significant reserves of copper, gold, coal, and chromite, though the proposed Memorandum of Understanding remains subject to final official approval.

stories.title: Pakistan and Turkmenistan Explore Strategies to Boost Bilateral Trade
stories.summary:
Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan and Turkmenistan’s Minister of Trade and Foreign Economic Relations, Dortguly Suleymanov, met in Islamabad on Monday to discuss methods for enhancing bilateral trade, regional connectivity, market access, and business cooperation. The meeting preceded the sixth session of the Pakistan–Turkmenistan Joint Intergovernmental Commission. Jam Kamal Khan emphasized developing practical partnerships in textiles, agriculture, food processing, manufacturing, and logistics, while noting that global freight disruptions make regional integration vital.

To improve connectivity, Jam Kamal Khan proposed direct flights and chartered cargo services between Islamabad and Ashgabat for time-sensitive agricultural exports. He also highlighted the expanding regional operations of Pakistan’s National Logistics Corporation and alternative trade routes for exports like Pakistani marble. Furthermore, he stressed the importance of business visa facilitation for investors and traders.

Turkmen Minister Dortguly Suleymanov addressed a recent decline in bilateral commerce, noting that trade turnover fell from over $36 million in 2025 down to roughly $15 million during the first nine months of 2026, primarily due to reduced textile exports. Both ministers agreed to nominate focal persons, such as Joint Secretary Maria for Pakistan, to coordinate trade-related matters. They also discussed updating exportable product lists, strengthening institutional ties, and boosting participation in international exhibitions.

Additionally, Jam Kamal Khan briefed his counterpart on Pakistan's five-year tariff rationalization program and the Ministry of Commerce's new online trade information portal. Both officials reaffirmed their commitment to achieving sustainable growth in economic relations through improved regional infrastructure and closer institutional coordination.

stories.title: State Bank of Pakistan Releases FY26 Report Highlighting Economic Resilience
stories.summary:
Pakistan’s central bank was compelled to raise its policy rate by 100 basis points in April after an energy shock driven by Middle East conflict pushed headline inflation into double digits, according to the State Bank of Pakistan's Governor’s Annual Report for FY26. Despite successive shocks including monsoon floods, trade tariff uncertainties, and geopolitical conflict, national economic indicators displayed resilience. Average national consumer price index inflation remained close to the upper bound of the medium-term target range, foreign exchange reserves surpassed targets, and real GDP recorded higher growth.

The report notes that average NCPI inflation was 5.5 percent from July to February 2026 before global oil price hikes pushed headline inflation into double digits from April onward. In response to the deteriorating inflation and external outlooks, the Monetary Policy Committee enacted the 100 basis point rate hike in April 2026 to contain secondary effects and maintain stability. Conversely, the SBP had reduced the rate by 50 basis points in December 2025 due to previously subdued inflation and stronger external accounts.

Regarding foreign exchange reserves, the SBP exceeded its target of $18 billion for the end of June 2026. The bank accomplished net foreign exchange purchases of $8.1 billion and reduced forward and swap liabilities by $1.6 billion, despite a moderate current account deficit. This reserve buildup, coupled with fiscal consolidation and successful International Monetary Fund reviews, improved sovereign ratings and exchange-rate stability.

The financial system maintained resilience as bank asset quality improved with a declining non-performing loan ratio, and capital adequacy ratios stayed well above regulatory requirements. Furthermore, the SBP pursued tertiary objectives by launching digital initiatives like the 'Zarkhez-e' agriculture lending platform, digital model villages, teen-accessible bank accounts, and the Pakistan Green Taxonomy.

stories.title: Autopsy Report Confirms Severe Torture of 13-Year-Old Domestic Worker
stories.summary:
The post-mortem report for 13-year-old domestic worker Fatima Asghar has confirmed she endured repeated and brutal physical torture before her death, sustaining at least 20 fresh and old injuries across her body. Released by the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences and handed over to the police, the autopsy details multiple wounds, bruises, scars, and signs of assault from her head to her feet. Investigators also observed severe swelling, blood clots in organs including the heart and kidneys, an old deteriorated wound on her left arm, and previous chest injuries.

Medical officers concluded that the cause of death was repeated physical assault resulting in severe inflammation, thromboembolism, and cardiopulmonary arrest. Preliminary investigations indicate the minor may have been subjected to abuse for approximately three years. The findings have also sparked questions regarding whether other individuals linked to the case were aware of the mistreatment.

Fatima was employed at the official residence of a senior Federal Investigation Agency officer stationed at the Police Lines Headquarters in Islamabad’s H-11 area. Legal experts have urged authorities to examine the roles of the FIA officer and the victim's father, while arguing that Section 328-A of the Pakistan Penal Code concerning cruelty to a child should be applied.
