The ongoing unwinding of the AI trade is serving as a major positive catalyst for the Indian market, effectively reversing negative trends that persisted for much of the year. While AI-heavy economies like South Korea and Taiwan face downward pressure, India has attracted investors seeking domestic growth drivers that appear insulated from the downturn in AI-related shares. This sentiment shift is reflected in foreign portfolio flows; foreign investors withdrew nearly $30 billion through October, marking 2026 as one of the worst years for flows, but November has witnessed a dramatic reversal with inflows approaching $10 billion, including over $500 million purchased on Monday alone.

Traders reported that dollar selling by foreign banks, likely connected to these new equity inflows, has successfully pushed the rupee back above the 94-per-dollar threshold. Additionally, lower crude oil prices have provided currency support, with crude settling down more than 3% amid signs of recovering shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. Although India's trade deficit widened to nearly $40 billion, market participants have largely overlooked the figure, viewing the recent surge in capital inflows as a more immediate economic driver.

stories.title: Trump Arrives in Manila for Quad Talks and Regional Summit Engagements
stories.summary:
US President Donald Trump travels to the Philippines on Tuesday for a Southeast Asian summit, where he is scheduled to attend the first meeting of the Quad alliance in two years. Trump's regional tour also includes the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen and an upcoming trilateral meeting with Chinese and Russian counterparts. The visit follows his Republican Party's defeat in midterm elections and ongoing spy allegations, factors that could complicate a delicate trade-war truce between Washington and Beijing. His arrival in Manila coincides with local demonstrations, which have featured the burning of presidential effigies, demands to end the Middle East conflict, and calls to scrap the US-led Pax Silica initiative.

The Quad meeting involving the United States, Japan, Australia, and India takes place two years after its previous gathering under former President Joe Biden. The summit occurs just before the APEC meeting hosted by Chinese President Xi Jinping, who has historically criticized the Quad as an attempt to encircle Beijing, though member nations maintain the group targets no specific country. During ASEAN meetings on Monday, Chinese Premier Li Qiang emphasized robust economic ties between China and ASEAN despite global trade restrictions. Meanwhile, members of the 11-member ASEAN bloc, which commands a combined GDP exceeding $3.9 trillion, seek deeper relations with the United States amidst ongoing diplomatic uncertainty.

Former US Deputy Secretary of State Kurt Campbell credited top US diplomat Marco Rubio with scheduling the Quad meeting to signal diplomatic strength ahead of the US-China-Russia talks. White House spokesperson Olivia Wales stated that under Trump, the Quad has acted as a partnership addressing regional challenges to ensure a free and open Indo-Pacific. Japanese officials indicated that discussions will likely center on maritime security, export restrictions, critical-minerals supply chains, and artificial intelligence. ASEAN will hold meetings with leaders from Japan, South Korea, China, and India ahead of the East Asia Summit.

While Trump will skip the main summit, he plans to attend a US-ASEAN Special Summit and meet Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Wednesday, alongside expected talks with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul to discuss a reciprocal trade agreement. The United States remains Thailand's largest export market, accounting for 24% of its shipments in 2026, and designated Thailand as a major non-NATO ally in 2003.

stories.title: بہرین میں عدالت نے ایران سے روابط پر 64 افراد کو سزائیں سنائیں
stories.summary:
بہرین کی ایک عدالت نے ایران کے ساتھ مبینہ روابط اور دہشت گردی کے الزامات کے تحت 64 افراد کو عمر قید اور دیگر سزاؤں کا حکم سنایا ہے۔ سزا پانے والوں میں 47 شیعہ علما بھی شامل ہیں، جبکہ منامہ کی ہائی کریمنل کورٹ نے پانچ دیگر افراد کو 15، 15 سال قید کی سزا دی ہے۔ بحرینی حکام کے مطابق یہ مقدمہ ایران کی اسلامی انقلابی گارڈ کور سے منسلک ایک دہشت گرد تنظیم قائم کرنے، نظامِ حکومت تبدیل کرنے کا مطالبہ کرنے اور ایران کے نظریے کو فروغ دینے کے الزامات پر چلایا گیا۔

برطانیہ میں قائم انسانی حقوق کی تنظیم 'بی آئی آر ڈی' نے ان فیصلوں اور مقدمے کی کارروائی کی شدید مذمت کی ہے۔ تنظیم کا کہنا ہے کہ مقدمے کے دوران ملزمان پر تشدد کیے جانے، زبردستی اعترافِ جرم کرانے اور دفاع کے مواقع محدود رکھنے کے سنگین الزامات سامنے آئے ہیں۔ انسانی حقوق کی متعدد بین الاقوامی تنظیموں نے بھی بحرینی حکام سے اس معاملے کی تحقیقات کا مطالبہ کیا تھا، کیونکہ فروری میں جنگ شروع ہونے کے بعد سے سینکڑوں افراد کو گرفتار کیا جا چکا ہے۔

اٹارنی جنرل اور دہشت گردی کے مقدمات کے استغاثہ کے سربراہ کے مطابق عدالت نے تمام ملزمان کو مجرم قرار دیتے ہوئے 15 سال سے لے کر عمر قید تک کی سزائیں سنائی ہیں۔ عدالت نے بعض افراد پر دو لاکھ 65 ہزار ڈالر جرمانہ عائد کیا اور دو کروڑ 12 لاکھ ڈالر ضبط کرنے کا بھی حکم دیا۔ سزا پانے والوں میں جلاوطن مذہبی رہنما آیت اللہ شیخ عیسیٰ قاسم سمیت تیرہ افراد ایسے ہیں جن کے خلاف ان کی غیر موجودگی میں مقدمہ چلایا گیا۔

بحرینی حکومت کے ترجمان نے تمام الزامات کی تردید کرتے ہوئے واضح کیا ہے کہ ملزمان کو مذہبی عقائد کی بنیاد پر نہیں بلکہ مجرمانہ سرگرمیوں میں ملوث ہونے کے ठोस شواہد کی بنیاد پر سزا دی گئی ہے۔ ترجمان کے مطابق کارروائی کے دوران تمام قانونی تقاضوں کو پورا کیا گیا اور حراست میں موجود افراد کو ان کے تمام قانونی حقوق اور طبی سہولتیں فراہم کی گئیں۔

stories.title: Israeli opposition slams Netanyahu over alleged election framing plot
stories.summary:
Israeli opposition figures have strongly condemned what they described as an attempted election coup following allegations that outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office tried to frame members of an Arab-Israeli party just before the legislative elections. According to reports from Channel 12, Netanyahu's chief of staff, Ido Norden, called the police on the eve of the October 27 election to complain about members of the Arab-Israeli Raam party. Norden allegedly directed officers to a purported intelligence source, who was a former employee of Netanyahu's office. This information led to the arrest of three Raam members, who were subsequently released after police found the allegations to be completely unfounded. Following these events, Netanyahu accused Arab parties of electoral fraud after they won a record number of seats in the vote.

Additional reports from the newspaper Haaretz revealed that David Zini, the head of the Shin Bet domestic security service, attempted to wiretap leaders of the Joint List, another Arab grouping, but the attorney general denied the request due to a lack of evidence. In response to the growing political scandal, Israeli police announced they would review their decision-making and information-transmission procedures. Meanwhile, political figures have reacted sharply to the revelations. Former opposition leader Yair Lapid and Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen both labeled the actions an attempted coup by Netanyahu. Raam’s number two official, Yoav Segalovitz, called for an urgent criminal investigation into the matter.

Netanyahu's Likud party dismissed the reports as utterly absurd, claiming the accusations were designed to block the formation of a national unity government. Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu's main rival and a former military chief of staff, stated that the caretaker prime minister posed a direct threat to Israeli democracy and could not remain in office for another minute. In last month's election, neither Netanyahu's bloc nor Eisenkot's opposition secured the necessary 61-seat majority required to govern. Both Raam and the Joint List have indicated their support for Eisenkot as political maneuvering continues in Jerusalem.

stories.title: Asian shares decline as US tech restrictions and Nvidia earnings loom
stories.summary:
Asian stock markets traded lower on Tuesday, dragged down by losses in the technology sector after the United States escalated efforts to restrict China's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips. South Korea's KOSPI dropped 2%, Taiwan's stocks fell 1.4%, Japan's Nikkei eased 1%, and MSCI's broad index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan declined 1.2%. The downturn followed Washington's announcement of new rules expanding restrictions on advanced AI chips to data centers in locations such as Thailand and Malaysia that Chinese entities have utilized to access computing power. The regulatory tightening follows recent scrutiny over the potential illegal diversion of advanced chips to China, compounding caution across global markets.

The regional tech selloff also coincided with upcoming quarterly earnings reports from Nvidia, with investors closely watching for indicators of future AI spending and market direction. In China and Hong Kong, markets similarly retreated, with the CSI300 blue-chip index down 0.5%, the Shanghai Composite dropping 0.65%, and the Hang Seng Tech Index losing about 2%. Concerns surrounding the broader outlook for artificial intelligence also impacted commodity markets, driving copper prices down to their lowest levels in over four months.

Concurrently, the US dollar strengthened, reaching its highest level since April 2025 by hitting 103.69 against a currency basket. The surge was driven by rising expectations of aggressive Federal Reserve interest rate hikes amid persistent inflationary pressures in the United States. The stronger dollar put downward pressure on other major currencies, pushing the euro to $1.0985 and leaving the Japanese yen struggling near the 160 level, which kept traders alert for potential currency intervention by authorities. Meanwhile, oil prices fell due to expectations of a growing supply surplus, with Brent crude down 0.9% to $91.62 a barrel.

stories.title: Ukraine, US, and European officials hold talks on future Russia negotiations
stories.summary:
Ukrainian, United States, and European negotiators have conducted their first joint discussions regarding future peace talks with Russia, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. Speaking on Monday, Zelensky noted that US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff participated in the online meeting, alongside representatives designated to speak for Europe. For the first time, the European continent was represented by negotiators from France, Britain, Germany, Poland, Italy, the European Union, and NATO. The diplomatic engagement comes as Russia continues to receive ballistic missile supplies from North Korea.

Jared Kushner confirmed the collaborative discussions, stating that the talks included national security advisers from European nations and that progress was being made to end the ongoing war. Kushner emphasized that a primary focus of the recent dialogue was finding ways to facilitate direct engagement between Kyiv and Moscow. While acknowledging that significant challenges remain and that a final agreement will require difficult decisions, Kushner expressed optimism that serious discussions away from the public spotlight are helping to narrow remaining gaps and explore potential solutions for lasting European security.

Simultaneously, President Zelensky warned that Russia is acquiring dozens of ballistic missiles per month from North Korea, urging European allies to supply more advanced weaponry to help Ukraine respond on equal terms. North Korea has emerged as one of Moscow's closest allies since the full-scale invasion began in 2022. Zelensky also cautioned citizens across Ukraine to remain vigilant regarding potential incoming missile strikes, vowing that every hostile action by Russia will receive a just response from Ukrainian forces.

stories.title: US dollar surges to 19-month high amid Federal Reserve rate expectations
stories.summary:
The US dollar climbed to a fresh 19-month peak against a basket of major currencies on Tuesday, buoyed by growing market expectations of more aggressive monetary policy tightening by the Federal Reserve. The currency's upward momentum was driven by a sharper-than-expected acceleration in US consumer inflation data released the previous week, leading to six consecutive days of gains for the US dollar index. The index reached 103.66, marking its highest level since April 2, 2025, when President Donald Trump introduced his tariff policies. The measure tracks the dollar against six international currencies, including the euro, British pound, and Japanese yen.

Financial markets have fully priced in a Federal Reserve interest rate hike at the upcoming December meeting, with the CME Group’s FedWatch tool indicating a small probability of an even larger half-point increase. This hawkish outlook has been further reinforced by strong economic data and central bank rhetoric. Analysts note that ongoing capital inflows related to the artificial intelligence boom have also provided underlying support for the US currency, though potential risks remain tied to unpredictable policy shifts and corrections in tech equities.

As the dollar strengthened, peer currencies experienced notable declines. The euro slipped to a 19-month low of $1.0985, the British pound fell to $1.3172, and the Swiss franc touched an 18-month high of 0.84075 against the dollar. The Japanese yen hovered near the critical 160 level per dollar, leaving market participants watchful for possible currency intervention by Japanese authorities. Meanwhile, the Australian dollar dipped to $0.6725, its lowest point since January, pressured by the broader risk-off sentiment in global markets.

stories.title: Gold prices hover near one-year low amid strong dollar and rate hike bets
stories.summary:
Gold prices held steady on Tuesday but remained close to their lowest level in more than a year. The stagnation is driven by a resilient US dollar and expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month. Investors are closely monitoring upcoming central bank meeting minutes for future monetary policy direction.

Spot gold traded little changed at $3,856.52 per ounce, following a drop on Monday to its lowest level since October 2025. Meanwhile, US gold futures for December delivery edged up 0.2% to $3,859. Bullion faced heavy losses due to high Treasury yields, a strong dollar, and anticipated monetary tightening, putting it on track for its worst performance in over ten years. The US dollar reached its highest level since April 2025, supported by strong inflation data and hawkish Fed commentary, which makes dollar-priced bullion more expensive for overseas buyers.

Market expectations point to a 96.6% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike in December, with only a 3.4% probability for a 50-basis-point move, based on CME’s FedWatch tool. Although gold traditionally serves as an inflation hedge, higher interest rates raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh noted that emerging technologies will significantly impact the economy, though outcomes could range from growth to higher unemployment. Traders are awaiting the minutes from the Fed’s October 27-28 Open Market Committee meeting on Wednesday for further policy insights.

Internationally, Bank of Japan board member Hajime Takata signaled that the central bank should raise its policy rate early to address mounting inflation risks, potentially as soon as December. Among other precious metals, spot silver steadied at $47.05 per ounce, platinum gained 0.1% to $1,450.75, and palladium rose 0.1% to $969.75. These global financial shifts continue to shape investor sentiment across various commodities.

stories.title: Oil prices decline on supply surplus outlook despite ongoing Gulf tensions
stories.summary:
Oil prices dropped on Tuesday as expectations of a supply surplus, driven by recovering Middle East exports, outweighed ongoing concerns about regional tanker attacks. Brent crude futures fell 44 cents, or 0.5%, to $92.00 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate futures also fell 44 cents, or 0.5%, to $85.28.

Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM Trade, noted that the oil market is recalibrating lower as supply catches up with and potentially exceeds demand. The International Energy Agency reported that the global oil market will return to a surplus in the fourth quarter, supported by faster-than-expected recovery in Middle East exports despite shipping attacks. Continued assaults on energy infrastructure and shipping lanes in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz maintain uncertainty, but geopolitical risk premiums are currently taking a back seat.

In policy developments, OPEC held an online meeting on Monday to review members' maximum sustainable production capacity. This exercise will help determine output quotas for the broader OPEC+ group, which includes Russia-led allies, ahead of their November 29 meeting on 2027 output policy. Iraq previously reported a $60 billion loss as Middle East conflicts impacted its oil exports.

Additionally, data from the US Department of Energy revealed that crude oil stocks in the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve dropped to 276.4 million barrels last week, marking the lowest level since August 1982. These recent drawdowns are part of a broader US agreement to release 172 million barrels from the facility.

stories.title: Karachi flour prices surge as wheat imports fail to offset national shortfall
stories.summary:
Wheat and wheat flour prices in Karachi have risen as imported grain arrivals fail to alleviate a persistent market shortfall. Retailers increased the price of flour No. 2.5 and fine flour by Rs10 per kg, reaching Rs180 and Rs200 per kg respectively, following rate hikes by local millers.

Since late October, over 100,000 tonnes of wheat have entered the country. The initial arrival of a 51,000-tonne shipment on October 28 temporarily pushed wheat down to Rs130 from Rs140 per kg, but open market grain prices reverted to Rs140 last week. Muzammil Chappal, Chairman of the Cereal Association of Pakistan, stated he warned the government in May about an impending four-million-tonne shortage and requested private sector imports of two million tonnes, requests that went unheeded. Despite a 4.3% rise in wheat production to 29.61 million tonnes in FY26, annual demand reaches 31 to 32 million tonnes due to a population growth rate exceeding 3% annually.

Wholesaler Rauf Ibrahim emphasized that the nation requires at least three million tonnes of wheat before new crops from Sindh and Punjab arrive between March and May. He criticized federal and provincial authorities for failing to target hoarders and speculators active in commodity investing. Millers adjusted prices for flour No. 2.5, Maida, and Fine Flour to Rs8,100, Rs9,000, and Rs9,150 per 50kg bag, up from Rs7,800, Rs8,400, and Rs8,550. High-quality Chakki flour reaches Rs200 in wholesale and Rs215 in retail markets.

The shortage affects low- and middle-income groups severely, with millers citing a lack of uniform pricing and inadequate imported supplies to meet daily Karachi grinding requirements of 80,000 bags. Meanwhile, tandoor owners face pressure from high flour and LPG costs, keeping prices for items like Chapati, Naan, and Sheermal unchanged for now at Rs20, Rs30-35, and Rs100-110.

stories.title: Pakistan wheat shortfall drives up flour prices despite new imports
stories.summary:
Consumer relief remains absent in Karachi as wheat and flour prices continue to climb amid an ongoing supply deficit. Retailers raised flour No. 2.5 and fine flour prices by Rs10 per kg to Rs180 and Rs200 per kg, following corresponding increases implemented by local flour millers.

More than 100,000 tonnes of wheat have arrived in Pakistan since the final week of October. The arrival of an initial ship carrying 51,000 tonnes on October 28 briefly reduced wheat prices to Rs130 from Rs140 per kg. However, open market rates returned to Rs140 per kg last week, prompting millers to elevate prices across various flour types. Cereal Association of Pakistan Chairman Muzammil Chappal noted he warned authorities in May about a potential four-million-tonne shortage and advocated for private sector imports of two million tonnes, but received no response. Official data from the Economic Survey FY26 shows wheat production increased by 4.3% to 29.61 million tonnes, yet annual demand stands between 31 and 32 million tonnes.

Trader Rauf Ibrahim noted that the country needs at least three million tonnes of wheat ahead of the next harvest season in Sindh and Punjab between March and May. He criticized governments for lacking effective campaigns against hoarders and speculators. Millers increased 50kg bag prices for flour No. 2.5, Maida, and Fine Flour to Rs8,100, Rs9,000, and Rs9,150, respectively. Premium Chakki flour sells at Rs200 per kg wholesale and Rs215 in retail.

Karachi mills face severe grain shortages as supplies from Punjab have halted and regional shipments remain delayed. Millers argue that imported volumes are vastly insufficient, noting that Karachi mills alone need 80,000 bags of 100kg daily. The crisis heavily impacts low- and middle-income households. Tandoor owners, dealing with high costs for both flour and LPG, have maintained current prices for Chapati, Naan, Sheermal, and Qulcha at Rs20, Rs30-35, Rs100-110, and Rs90-100.

stories.title: FBI assists Sri Lanka in cracking down on cyber scam operations
stories.summary:
The Federal Bureau of Investigation is providing assistance to Sri Lankan law enforcement to detect and disrupt transnational cyber scam networks. The US embassy in Colombo announced the partnership on Monday, noting that criminal syndicates have increasingly relocated their illicit operations to the island nation following crackdowns in several Southeast Asian countries. 

Sri Lanka has emerged as an attractive destination for these fraud compounds due to its relaxed visa regulations and reliable, high-speed internet infrastructure. As part of the initiative, an FBI team is spending a week in Sri Lanka this month to train local investigators in advanced investigative techniques, digital forensics, and case development. The training aims to help authorities identify victims, trace criminal financial activity, and build robust legal cases against perpetrators. 

Fraud compounds typically lure internet users into fake romantic relationships, fraudulent cryptocurrency investments, and illegal betting platforms. While some participants are willing actors, others are trafficked foreign nationals coerced into working in these facilities. These criminal networks primarily target victims across Asia, including individuals in India, Vietnam, and the Philippines, raising local concerns that Sri Lankans could also be targeted. 

Since the beginning of the year, Sri Lankan authorities have arrested more than 1,100 foreign nationals—predominantly from China, Vietnam, and India—for suspected involvement in cybercrime. In addition to US assistance, Sri Lanka has sought cooperation from China, which previously noted an increase in illicit operations within the country after crackdowns in Cambodia, Myanmar, and the United Arab Emirates.

stories.title: State Bank of Pakistan Reports Economic Resilience Amid Global Shocks
stories.summary:
Pakistan’s economy displayed resilience against various domestic and global shocks throughout the 2025-26 fiscal year, according to the State Bank of Pakistan's annual report. Despite challenges such as shifting United States trade tariffs, early monsoon flooding, and a Middle East conflict that began in late February 2026, the country maintained overall macroeconomic stability backed by stronger fiscal and external buffers. Real gross domestic product growth rose to 3.7 percent, driven largely by a rebound in large-as-scale manufacturing output.

The central bank noted that prudent monetary policies, ongoing fiscal consolidation, and structural reforms implemented under an International Monetary Fund program helped safeguard stability. Austerity measures and the passing on of higher global oil prices to domestic consumers successfully contained external shocks on accounts. Additionally, growing workers' remittances kept the current account deficit down to 0.1 percent of gross domestic product, while foreign exchange reserves benefited from official inflows, successful bond issuances, and foreign exchange purchases by the bank.

Despite these positive indicators, the State Bank of Pakistan emphasized the critical need for deep-rooted structural reforms to achieve sustainable, high economic growth. The report highlighted challenges in job creation, pointing to volatile gross domestic product growth, low female labor participation, high youth unemployment, and widespread informal employment. It also addressed emerging pressures from Industry 4.0, green transitions, and climate change impacts on agriculture.

To secure long-term stability and foster investments, the bank recommended encouraging private sector participation, improving infrastructure, enhancing skills development, and rationalizing taxes. It also urged the adoption of rules-based economic frameworks to reduce policy uncertainty. Implementing these measures is viewed as essential for supporting the expanding working-age population and reducing vulnerability to future supply chain disruptions.

stories.title: Government Allocates Rs300 Billion for SMEs Under Export Finance Scheme
stories.summary:
Pakistan's government has set aside Rs300 billion exclusively for small and medium enterprises under its short-term Export Finance Scheme. The announcement was made during an Islamabad meeting chaired by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, which focused on reviewing progress regarding export finance initiatives and the recently introduced SME Connect Portal.

During the session, the State Bank of Pakistan delivered a presentation on the SME Connect Portal, which was launched on November 1, 2026. The digital platform is designed to increase transparency and ease bank financing by allowing smaller businesses to register profiles, submit financing requests, and monitor application statuses. Officials noted that the system enables systematic tracking of bank responses and processing timelines, though institutions will continue utilizing their own lending policies.

The Export-Import Bank of Pakistan also briefed participants on export financing initiatives, detailing how the Rs300 billion allocation will support working capital requirements and export activities for smaller enterprises. Discussions additionally covered improving long-term financing access to stimulate investment in export-oriented projects and business expansion.

Finance Minister Aurangzeb stressed the importance of robust coordination among institutions to ensure credit reaches smaller and export-oriented businesses. Attendees included several federal ministers, the governor of the State Bank of Pakistan, the chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan, and other senior officials.

stories.title: Pakistan and Turkmenistan to Focus on TAPI Gas Pipeline Project
stories.summary:
The Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India natural gas pipeline project is set to take center stage during the Sixth Pakistan-Turkmenistan Joint Intergovernmental Commission meeting in Islamabad. The strategic regional energy initiative aims to transport natural gas from Turkmenistan through Afghanistan and Pakistan to India, reinforcing regional connectivity and long-term energy security.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar will co-chair the session alongside Turkmenistan's Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Rashid Meredov, who leads a high-level delegation. The meeting serves to review the entire scope of bilateral economic cooperation, spanning trade, investment, energy, agriculture, transport, and higher education.

In addition to the TAPI pipeline, the two sides will discuss progress on the proposed Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan electricity transmission project. Separate bilateral talks between the two foreign ministers are also scheduled on the sidelines to examine regional and international developments of mutual interest.

The upcoming session marks the first time the commission has convened since its fifth session in Ashgabat in August 2017. Both nations aim to translate their longstanding diplomatic relations into tangible economic partnerships and stronger institutional cooperation.

stories.title: Pakistan Shaheens Depart for ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Shaheens cricket squad departed from Karachi for Doha, Qatar, to compete in the 50-over ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026. Running from November 19 to 29, the tournament features a 15-member visiting squad captained by Abdul Samad. Ali Raza and Farhan Yousuf will join the team directly in Doha after recently participating in the under-19 Asia Cup in Oman.

As defending champions, Pakistan is placed in Group B alongside India 'A', Nepal, and the United Arab Emirates. The team's campaign opens against the United Arab Emirates on November 20, followed by fixtures against India 'A' on November 22 and Nepal on November 24. Subsequent matches include the semi-finals on November 26 and 27, and the final on November 29 at the West End Park International Cricket Stadium.

Ahead of their departure, captain Abdul Samad expressed confidence in the team's preparations, noting that the squad completed a week of scenario-based matches and intensive training with the coaching staff. He emphasized the importance of maintaining momentum starting from the opening fixture and ensuring every player executes their designated role effectively.

Pakistan previously claimed the 50-over title in 2023 by defeating India 'A' by 128 runs in Sri Lanka. The support staff accompanying the squad includes head coach and team manager Ijaz Ahmed Jr., batting coach Riffatullah Mohmand, and bowling coach Rehan Riaz.

stories.title: Punjab Government Plans Anti-Rape Law and Fast-Track Courts
stories.summary:
The Punjab government has announced plans to implement an anti-rape law alongside fast-track courts to guarantee rapid trials for crimes against women and children, complete with strict timelines for resolution. The initiative was unveiled during a Lahore meeting on November 16, led by Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, aimed at upgrading the regional criminal justice system and boosting protections for vulnerable demographics. Officials emphasized that specialized investigations and proactive reporting mechanisms are vital for increasing conviction rates and preventing offenders from evading justice.

During the briefing, Inspector General of Police Rao Abdul Karim reported that approximately 1.24 million complaints regarding women have been filed across Punjab police stations, with 92 percent resolved. Additionally, the Women Virtual Police Station handled roughly 125,000 complaints, while the Virtual Centre for Child Safety successfully located over 70,000 missing or abducted children. Authorities also reunited 4,000 special needs children with their families and solved 7,588 child sexual abuse cases throughout the chief minister's current tenure.

Despite these efforts, officials expressed alarm over data showing that individuals known to the victims were responsible for 71 percent of documented sexual abuse cases involving women and children. In response, Chief Minister Nawaz urged the expansion of public awareness campaigns and mandated that police enhance their investigative capacities. She also stressed the adoption of artificial intelligence to improve evidence collection, audio-video preservation, and overall prosecution quality.

While a federal framework called the Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act, 2021, already exists, it remains undetermined whether provincial legislators will adopt its specific provisions or draft a custom framework tailored directly to Punjab's unique requirements. The renewed focus on legal reforms underscores the administration's stated priority to tackle low conviction rates and curb escalating violence against women and children across the province.

stories.title: Houthi Forces Advance Toward Aden as Saudi Coalition Shakes Up Leadership
stories.summary:
Yemeni military sources reported that Houthi fighters have captured strategic ground on Yemen's southern coast after Saudi-backed government forces fell back to fortify Aden. The retreat follows a Yemeni government announcement on Sunday to withdraw from areas near the Bab al-Mandeb Strait following an October counterattack. Five military sources confirmed that Houthi units advanced to Khor Omairh, situated roughly 100 kilometers west of Aden, positioning themselves 25 kilometers from government defensive lines at Qawah. Additional reports indicated that insurgents reached a position 60 kilometers from Aden, which serves as the seat of government power.

Amid these mounting battlefield reverses, Saudi Arabia replaced the commander of its military coalition. A royal decree issued on Monday named Chief of Staff General Fayyad bin Hamed bin Ruqad al-Ruwaili as the new coalition commander, replacing Lieutenant General Fahd bin Hamad bin Abdulaziz Al-Salman, who was reassigned as a military adviser to the defense minister. Analysts noted that the command shuffle reflects ongoing frustration with the fragmented nature and recurring coordination failures of allied Yemeni forces facing unified Houthi opposition.

Residents in Aden voiced mounting anxiety regarding the approaching conflict. Local witnesses reported that government security forces have established numerous checkpoints and intensified identity checks throughout the port city. Although fuel and food supplies remain accessible, citizens remain apprehensive about the retreating lines. Government officials indicated that redeploying units aim to secure Aden and Lahj province while preparing to reclaim lost territory.

The broader conflict reignited over the summer as a spillover of wider hostilities involving the United States, Israel, and Iran. Following the collapse of a 2022 truce in July, Houthi forces launched rapid offensives in September, seizing Red Sea coastal areas and besieging Taiz. Analysts remain skeptical that replacing leadership at the top of the Saudi coalition will resolve the structural divisions plaguing anti-Houthi forces on the ground.

stories.title: Pakistan Finance Ministry Orders Strict Minimum Wage Compliance Across Public Sector
stories.summary:
Acting on directives from a parliamentary committee, Pakistan's Ministry of Finance has instructed all ministries and divisions to guarantee that minimum wages are paid to employees across attached departments, autonomous corporations, and subordinate organizations. An official office memorandum distributed by the ministry requested written confirmation that mandated salaries are disbursed exclusively through banking channels. Ministries were explicitly directed to enforce government wage policies thoroughly and submit formal compliance reports.

This administrative action stems from persistent concerns raised by the National Assembly’s Standing Committee on Overseas Pakistanis and Human Resource Development regarding widespread non-compliance within public sector entities. Committee members previously criticized public organizations for failing to implement revised minimum daily wage rates, noting that such delays set a poor precedent that encourages private employers to bypass legal standards. Special attention was drawn to the Overseas Pakistanis Foundation, where employees waited four months for salary adjustments despite budgetary approval for the 2026-27 fiscal year.
P
arliamentarians expressed strong displeasure over administrative double standards, contrasting the prompt implementation of salary increases for high-ranking officers in grades 20 to 22 with the prolonged delays experienced by low-paid workers awaiting board approvals. To rectify these disparities, the committee recommended instituting new regulations to ensure revised minimum wages take effect immediately upon announcement. Furthermore, the committee advised the Finance Ministry to place workers' welfare funds into interest-bearing accounts so that generated returns can directly benefit the workforce.

stories.title: BISP Board Approves Financial Assistance for Unmarried Women Aged 45 and Above
stories.summary:
The Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) has expanded its eligibility criteria to include unmarried women who are 45 years of age or older. BISP Chairperson Senator Rubina Khalid announced this policy update during a press conference in Lahore on Monday, explaining that the decision was recently approved by the BISP Board.

Providing details on the scale of the national welfare initiative, Senator Khalid noted that out of more than 10 million beneficiary families nationwide, roughly five million reside in Punjab. She emphasized that the programme operates as a nationwide social safety net catering to eligible families regardless of their political affiliation.

In addition to widening the beneficiary bracket, the chairperson highlighted the implementation of a modern digital payment framework. By introducing digital mobile wallets and an interoperable payment infrastructure through 1-LINK and six partner banks, recipients are no longer bound to collect their stipends from specific distribution centres.

To facilitate the transition, enrolled women have been issued free SIM cards alongside activated digital wallet accounts tied to their names. Beneficiaries now receive automated SMS notifications whenever funds are successfully credited, allowing them to track and withdraw their financial aid more conveniently and transparently.

stories.title: Faisalabad Buffalo Wins Livestock Competition with Record Milk Yield
stories.summary:
A buffalo named Morni, owned by Rana Ikram from Faisalabad, secured first place in a local livestock department competition held on Monday in Chak 100-JB. The winning animal yielded 49.4 kilograms of milk, earning its owner a cash prize of one million rupees.

In the same primary category, buffaloes belonging to Arham Gujjar from Sahiwal and Rana Adeel from Faisalabad tied for second place with a milk output of 44.2 kilograms each. They shared a prize consisting of half a million rupees and a 125cc motorcycle. Meanwhile, a buffalo owned by Malik Saif Awan of Lahore claimed third place by producing 43.2 kilograms of milk, receiving a 70cc Honda motorcycle.

Rana Ikram also dominated a secondary category of the contest. Another of his buffaloes yielded 38.6 kilograms to win a 125cc motorbike, while two more of his animals secured third and fourth places with yields of 33.9 kilograms and 31 kilograms, respectively. Rana Abdul Rehman of Chak 208-RB took second place in this category with a 36.7-kilogram yield.

The event was attended by Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah as the special guest, alongside MPAs Zafar Iqbal Nagra and Haji Shaukat Dogar, and Deputy Director Livestock Dr Sohail Anjum.

stories.title: Sindh Minister Sharjeel Memon Stresses Referendum Lacks Legal Standing for New Provinces
stories.summary:
Sindh Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon asserted on Monday that holding a referendum on carving out new provinces holds no legal or constitutional ground. Addressing a press conference in Karachi, he maintained that the provincial assembly has already delivered its official verdict regarding any division of Sindh.

Highlighting the constitutional framework, Mr Memon stated that any proposal to create a new province requires a two-thirds majority vote from the provincial assembly belonging to the affected region. He cautioned against political parties attempting to stir ethnic and linguistic divisions, reaffirming that the provincial government will firmly prevent such actions.

Regarding planned political rallies in Karachi, the senior minister underscored that organizers must secure prior government authorization. He stated that entities failing to obtain proper permission or attempting to impose unauthorized venues and dates will be barred from holding public gatherings, though peaceful political activities remain welcome under established rules.

Shifting to development initiatives, Mr Memon spotlighted the province's post-flood housing efforts, describing the two-billion-dollar undertaking as the world's largest housing project for poor families. He reported that over one million homes have been finished, construction is underway for another 700,000, and dozens of rural committees have been formed to oversee rehabilitation while ensuring significant female representation.

stories.title: Pakistan Sugar Mills Association Demands Immediate Export Permission and Deregulation
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Sugar Mills Association (PSMA) has called on the government to instantly grant permission for sugar exports, completely deregulate the industry, and retract mandatory orders forcing mills to initiate sugarcane crushing instantly. PSMA Chairman Asim Ghani Usman made these demands during a press conference in Lahore on Monday, warning that the sector faces severe financial distress.

According to the association, the country currently holds an estimated surplus of 1.1 million tonnes of sugar. Although the government previously committed to allowing the export of 600,000 tonnes, millers report that no formal authorization has been issued despite repeated follow-ups. Furthermore, sugarcane cultivation has expanded by roughly 16 per cent this season, pushing projected sugar production for the 2026-27 crushing season to 8.5 million tonnes.

Addressing the Punjab government's directive requiring mills to commence crushing operations within 24 hours, Mr Usman argued that the timeline is practically impossible to fulfill. He explained that preparing a sugar mill involves recalling staff and firing up large boilers, a process that requires adequate lead time.

Additionally, farmers need a reasonable window to harvest their crops. Consequently, the association has formally requested the chief minister to review the situation and grant a 15-day extension for mills to safely begin operations.

stories.title: Government Increases Export Finance Scheme Funding to Rs1.5 Trillion
stories.summary:
The government has elevated total funding under the Export Finance Scheme from one trillion rupees to 1.5 trillion rupees, dedicating 300 billion rupees specifically for new exporters and smaller businesses. These updated schemes officially went into effect on November 1 and were examined during a ministry session on Monday. Federal ministers and division secretaries participated in the gathering, which was directed by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb.

As part of these adjustments aimed at bolstering export-driven expansion, authorities elevated the collateral-free borrowing threshold for small and medium enterprises from ten million rupees to 50 million rupees. Official data shows that total outstanding financing for smaller enterprises climbed from 691 billion rupees in June 2025 to 1.114 trillion rupees by June 2026, eventually reaching 1.148 trillion rupees in October. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif established a 2.2 trillion rupee objective for this sector by 2028, alongside distinct targets set by the central bank and finance ministry.

During the session, the State Bank of Pakistan delivered an update regarding the performance of the SME Connect Portal, which debuted on November 1. This centralized platform allows businesses to register company profiles, submit funding applications, and track progress transparently. Minister Aurangzeb noted that the digital system enhances oversight of financial institutions and ensures that processing timelines are strictly monitored.

The finance minister stressed the vital role that smaller enterprises play in driving local economic activity, generating investments, and creating employment opportunities. He highlighted the necessity of broadening financial inclusion so that smaller and export-focused commercial operations can readily secure necessary capital. Additionally, the administration intends to expand the total count of smaller business borrowers from approximately 350,862 registered in September to 775,000 by June 2028.

stories.title: ECO Endorses Regional Peace Initiatives and Praises Pakistan's Mediation
stories.summary:
Member states of the Economic Cooperation Organisation have officially endorsed diplomatic initiatives by Pakistan, Qatar, and Iran aimed at securing a permanent conclusion to the US-Iran war. During the 30th meeting of the ECO Council of Ministers in Islamabad, the bloc adopted the Islamabad Communiqué, which praised the mediation roles undertaken by Pakistan and Qatar alongside Iran's recent peace efforts. The meeting was chaired by Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, marking the beginning of Pakistan's 2026-27 chairmanship under the theme "Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO."

The communiqué highlighted the challenging geopolitical climate while commending Pakistan's constructive diplomatic support, the Islamabad Peace Talks, a resulting Memorandum of Understanding, and subsequent negotiations in Burgenstock, Switzerland. Furthermore, the participants rejected unilateral coercive measures, economic pressures, and sanctions, stating they violate international law and the United Nations Charter. The ministers also addressed the humanitarian situation in Gaza, calling for urgent deliveries of food, medicine, winter clothing, and fuel following flooding in Deir al-Balah on November 6, while demanding adherence to the October 2025 Gaza ceasefire agreement.

Beyond political security, the gathering outlined a broad economic roadmap, including the adoption of the Strategic Goals of Economic Cooperation 2035 and advancements to the ECO Trade Agreement to drive regional integration and market connectivity. Member states emphasized improving transportation corridors, customs simplification, and establishing joint trade zones. Additional areas of regional collaboration involved energy security, clean energy initiatives centered around the ECO Clean Energy Centre in Baku, artificial intelligence technologies, and joint actions on water conservation and climate-resilient agriculture.

This high-level ministerial meeting matters because it demonstrates a collective regional commitment to diplomatic conflict resolution, economic resilience, and coordinated humanitarian responses amid severe geopolitical tensions. By solidifying institutional strategies through 2035 and positioning Pakistan at the helm for 2026-27, the ECO aims to fortify cross-border trade, transportation networks, and sustainable development across member countries while advocating for stability in both South Asia and the broader Middle East.

stories.title: Iran Bars Nuclear Inspections Until Regional War Ends
stories.summary:
A senior Iranian official announced that Tehran will block United Nations inspectors from visiting damaged nuclear installations until the ongoing Middle East conflict concludes and United States conditions are satisfied. Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi made the televised statement on Sunday, responding to demands from the International Atomic Energy Agency to resume inspections suspended since last year's conflict with Israel. Gharibabadi asserted that IAEA requests are primarily intended to assess the physical effectiveness of American weaponry used during strikes against sites such as Natanz, Fordow, and Isfahan.

The standoff runs parallel to escalating maritime hostilities in the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran has restricted vessel traffic. Maritime monitors reported that a Panama-flagged oil tanker, the ON PHOENIX, caught fire after being struck by an unknown projectile near the Omani coast, though all crew members escaped safely. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps subsequently claimed that multiple vessels have struck naval mines within the strait, stating that six tankers have sunk or caught fire since Sunday. The Iranian army also confirmed that another tanker was immobilized after striking a mine in the eastern sector of the waterway.

Geopolitical tensions intensified further with the arrival of the USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier group in the Middle East on Sunday, raising the total number of deployed US carrier strike groups to three. The deployment follows recent drone attacks targeting US-allied Bahrain and a broader lack of diplomatic progress toward ending hostilities. Tehran continues to demand the unfreezing of assets and the lifting of economic sanctions as prerequisites for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, maintaining that broader nuclear negotiations will only be addressed at a later stage.

stories.title: Seventeen People Killed Across Two Separate Mass Shootings in South Africa
stories.summary:
Seventeen individuals lost their lives in two separate mass shooting incidents in South Africa, according to police statements on Monday. The nation, which struggles with persistently high murder rates, saw these violent attacks unfold in different regions over the weekend.

In the first incident, authorities discovered nine bodies inside a shack in an informal settlement situated outside the capital of Pretoria on Monday morning. The victims, consisting of six men and three women, all sustained gunshot wounds. Provincial police commissioner Tommy Mthombeni indicated that this specific attack might be connected to a previous shooting from last year in a nearby informal settlement that left twelve people dead and thirteen others wounded.

The second mass killing occurred outside the eastern city of Pietermaritzburg within a semi-rural location. Responding to shooting reports on Sunday, officers found a bullet-riddled vehicle containing eight dead men who had multiple gunshot wounds. KwaZulu-Natal province police spokesman Colonel Robert Netshiunda stated that the victims were estimated to be between 20 and 30 years old and remained unidentified, while noting it was premature to speculate on a motive. Netshiunda also mentioned that historical triggers for such local violence range from stock theft and drugs to disputes involving the taxi industry.

Thamsanqa Ntuli, the premier of the province, attributed the horrific violence to the widespread availability and proliferation of illegal firearms. Ntuli highlighted this easy access to weapons as one of the most significant security threats facing the region today. Authorities continue to investigate both mass casualty events as the country deals with the ongoing challenge of high levels of violent crime.

stories.title: State Bank of Pakistan Projects GDP Growth Between 3.5 and 4.5 Percent
stories.summary:
Pakistan anticipates steady economic progress in fiscal year 2027, with the State Bank of Pakistan estimating real gross domestic product growth to fall within 3.5 to 4.5 percent. Released on Monday, the central bank's annual report on the economy attributes this positive outlook to enhanced macroeconomic stability, revived domestic demand, previous monetary easing, and reinforced fiscal and external buffers alongside industrial activity measures.

The country entered the fiscal year on stronger ground, displaying resilience against global supply disruptions and rising input expenses driven by ongoing Middle East tensions. Continued engagement with the International Monetary Fund and upgraded sovereign credit ratings have bolstered investor sentiment and lowered the national risk premium. The central bank noted that the economy has absorbed these external shocks better than during the Russia-Ukraine conflict in fiscal year 2022.

Despite these positive indicators, the economic outlook faces downside risks from climate change, new trade blocks, and Middle East hostilities. Agricultural prospects are threatened by worsening El Niño patterns, though outputs for staple kharif crops like rice, maize, and sugarcane have increased compared to the previous year. Commodity sector improvements are expected to stimulate the services industry, while worker remittances will likely keep the current account deficit between 0 and 1.0 percent of GDP.

Government fiscal consolidation and power sector reforms are anticipated to moderate expenditures in fiscal year 2027. Meanwhile, enhanced tax collection efforts and broader tax bases are projected to keep the fiscal deficit between 3 and 4 percent of GDP. The State Bank of Pakistan remains dedicated to maintaining price stability, securing the financial system, and fostering sustainable growth through data-driven policies.

stories.title: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif Urges the OIC to Take Stronger Action
stories.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with the newly appointed Organisation of Islamic Cooperation Secretary-General, Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed, in Islamabad on Monday. During the discussions, the prime minister called on the 57-member organization to move past diplomatic rhetoric and adopt a more proactive and effective stance in addressing severe crises across the Muslim world, notably focusing on Palestine and Indian Occupied Jammu and Kashmir.

Welcoming Ahmed on his first visit to Pakistan since taking office, Sharif congratulated him on his unanimous election, noting that it demonstrated the deep confidence placed in him by member states. He also pledged that Pakistan would persistently support the organization and actively contribute to advancing the shared objectives of Muslim nations.

In response, the secretary-general acknowledged Pakistan's ongoing contributions toward fostering regional peace and stability. Both leaders evaluated strategies to enhance the organization's global influence, foster better coordination among member countries, and deliver more robust responses to collective humanitarian and political challenges.

The meeting concluded with a mutual reaffirmation of support for the Palestinian and Kashmiri populations, emphasizing that their respective struggles remain core priorities on the diplomatic agenda of the organization.

stories.title: Pakistan Approves SME Export Facilitation Centres in Four Major Cities
stories.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif approved the creation of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises facilitation centres in four major urban areas during a meeting in Islamabad on Monday. Operating as a pilot project, these centers will be set up in Karachi, Lahore, Peshawar, and Quetta, with plans to expand the initiative nationwide following performance reviews.

Addressing a delegation of small and medium-sized exporters, the prime minister described these enterprises as the backbone of the national economy, emphasizing that facilitating their entry into global export markets is a core government priority. He instructed relevant officials to quickly develop an action plan for a sustainable cold-storage infrastructure to support perishable goods exports.

Regarding financial support, Sharif noted that 300 billion rupees have been allocated under the Export Finance Scheme specifically for small and medium-sized businesses and new exporters, with the Export-Import Bank of Pakistan issuing a circular to enforce this exclusive reservation. Additionally, he approved the modernization of the Trade Development Authority of Pakistan and the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority to help domestic industries meet international standards.

Delegation members welcomed these measures and offered practical suggestions to resolve exporter challenges. The prime minister subsequently formed a committee to review these recommendations and report on their implementation. Senior government officials, cabinet ministers, and the governor of the State Bank of Pakistan attended the session.

stories.title: State Bank of Pakistan Projects Inflation to Exceed Target Range
stories.summary:
The State Bank of Pakistan expects inflation to stay above its medium-term target range through fiscal year 2027 due to ongoing global energy price shocks and climbing input expenses. According to the central bank's annual report, average national Consumer Price Index inflation is forecasted between 5.5 and 7.5 percent, slightly higher than the official government target range of 5 to 7 percent. This projection utilizes an assumed oil price of 80 US dollars per barrel and will be reviewed in January 2027.

Global energy price fluctuations prompted the government to transition from fortnightly to weekly petroleum price reviews in March 2026, followed by daily price adjustments starting in July 2026. These daily modifications allowed for a smoother pass-through of international oil price shifts. Additionally, the government permitted wheat imports to alleviate domestic food supply limitations while maintaining a prudent monetary policy to anchor inflation expectations.

The outbreak of conflict in the Middle East during late February 2026 introduced substantial upward risks, causing sharp increases in global fuel prices, freight expenses, and transport disruptions. Consequently, the Monetary Policy Committee raised the policy rate by 100 basis points to 11.5 percent in April 2026 to counter second-round effects from oil shocks. Average inflation reached 7.1 percent in fiscal year 2026, rising from 4.5 percent the previous year, managed largely by coordinated monetary tightening and fiscal consolidation.

stories.title: Regulator Increases Incremental Consumption Package Rate Amid Unverified Marginal Costs
stories.summary:
The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority has implemented a provisional increase in the Incremental Consumption Package rate, lifting industrial and agricultural charges from Rs22.98 to Rs25.30 per unit. This regulatory adjustment is notable because the oversight body acknowledges that the foundational marginal cost remains unverified. Originally introduced in December 2025, the scheme aims to encourage additional industrial and agricultural demand to utilize unused generating capacity that continues to attract fixed costs. The package was structured around six-monthly reviews to guarantee that revenue generated from extra units adequately covers the associated supply expenses, with the Power Division assigned to provide the necessary economic analyses.

When the initial review period arrived, the Power Division submitted incomplete data, failed to deliver proper cost calculations, and ultimately suggested that NEPRA conduct the evaluation itself. This refusal by the institution that originally designed the policy sparked criticism, especially given the scale of the oversight. The regulator analyzed approximately 3,969 gigawatt-hours of incremental consumption, yielding a tentative consumer-end marginal cost of Rs29.65 per unit. However, authorities considered this figure unreliable because generation records, operational assumptions, and fuel-cost adjustments were never properly reconciled. Instead of calculating actual metrics, the Power Division's Rs25.30 proposal simply updated fuel prices while retaining the generation mix from the scheme's original design.

Internal disagreements plagued NEPRA regarding the decision, as two members advocated for suspending the package until verifiable cost data became available. Ultimately, the chairman utilized a casting vote to maintain the programme provisionally while demanding the outstanding analysis. This choice preserves an industrial incentive, but it leaves authorities defending a price lacking a firm economic foundation. Furthermore, risks extend to consumers outside the program. If electricity supplied under the incentive costs more than beneficiaries pay, the difference can be absorbed into fuel-cost adjustments borne by regular customers, shifting financial burdens onto those who never received preferential rates through an insufficiently transparent billing system.

Critics argue that officials frequently blame external constraints like the IMF for energy-sector issues, even though international lenders do not prepare missing reviews or rely on outdated generation assumptions. Those responsibilities rest strictly with domestic institutions. To address the transparency gap, NEPRA established deadlines of November 25 and December 3 for comprehensive modeling and reconciled cost data, emphasizing that results must be publicized. If the scheme fails to demonstrate genuine cost-reflectivity, authorities must reconsider its continuation, as the nation cannot sustain an electricity policy driven by guesswork and unverified calculations.

stories.title: Pakistan Records Rise in Exports and Widening Trade Deficit in Early Fiscal Year
stories.summary:
According to the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, national exports reached 11.4 billion dollars during the first four months, spanning July to October, of the current fiscal year. This represents an 8.8 percent increase compared to the 10.4 billion dollars recorded during the corresponding period of the previous year. Official press releases attribute this upward trend to the government's focus on export-led economic growth, championed by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif through direct engagement with industrialists, exporters, and business representatives. However, analysts emphasize that evaluating this revenue growth requires clarifying whether the gains stem from higher export volumes or are simply the result of elevated global inflationary pressures following the February 28 US-Israeli attack on Iran and subsequent reductions in Gulf petroleum and gas exports.

Simultaneously, the data revealed a 12.59 percent rise in total imports during the July-October 2026 period, climbing from 23,060 million dollars to 25,964 million dollars compared to the previous year. Clarity is similarly required regarding whether import expenses increased due to higher global input costs or the relaxation of administrative measures. Authorities previously instituted these restrictions to curb imports and protect the balance of payments. While easing these controls aims to stimulate growth by facilitating the acquisition of raw materials and semi-finished products, it frequently triggers the boom-bust cycles that force successive administrations to seek assistance from the International Monetary Fund.

Consequently, the trade imbalance widened from negative 12.6614 billion dollars in the first four months of last year to negative 15.628 billion dollars in the current period, reflecting a 15.97 percent increase. This widening deficit is double the growth rate of exports and exceeds import growth by three percentage points, supporting concerns that the balance of payments position is deteriorating. Such trends suggest administrative interventions might soon be necessary. If these trade imbalances persist after the conclusion of the current IMF arrangement next September, the country risks entering a twenty-sixth loan program with the international financial body.

Furthermore, government leverage to grant tax concessions or export incentives remains severely constrained under the ongoing IMF framework. In its September 2024 documents, the Fund highlighted that widespread protectionism, subsidies, and tax concessions have historically undermined Pakistan's tax base, market competition, and productivity. With exporters demanding historical incentives that the administration cannot legally or financially provide, the expanding trade deficit signals a potential return to economic volatility. Experts argue that addressing these systemic vulnerabilities requires deep structural changes to the domestic production base, shifting policy toward producing specifically for export rather than merely offloading excess domestic surplus.

stories.title: Germany Crushes Netherlands Five-Nil to Reach Nations League Quarter-Finals
stories.summary:
Germany delivered a commanding performance on Monday at the Olympiastadion in Berlin, routing the Netherlands 5-0 in a UEFA Nations League Group A2 fixture to secure a spot in the quarter-finals. Florian Wirtz scored two goals, while Brajan Gruda contributed a goal and two assists. Derry Scherhant and Nico Schlotterbeck also scored, completing the largest victory for Germany over their neighbors since a 7-0 triumph in 1959. The win marked the most impressive match of coach Jurgen Klopp’s six-game tenure, leaving the German side jubilant as they advanced alongside the Dutch.

The match began cautiously with both teams playing a risk-averse style, though the Netherlands squandered an early opportunity when Crysencio Summerville lost his footing in front of the goal. Germany broke the deadlock just before halftime when Berlin-born Scherhant curled a precise shot inside the far post. Following the interval, the home side dominated completely. Wirtz extended the lead with an intricate solo effort on the hour mark before Schlotterbeck headed in a free-kick from Gruda just five minutes later. Gruda then set up Wirtz for his second goal and subsequently tapped in a rebounding shot himself to cap off the rout.

Despite the heavy defeat, the Netherlands still qualified for the final eight of the tournament, though the late German goals pushed them down to second place in the group standings. Dutch coach Xavi Hernandez apologized to supporters for the team's poor performance, citing a lack of speed and defensive organization, compounded by the absence of injured captain Virgil van Dijk. Meanwhile, coach Klopp praised the immense work rate of debutants Gruda and Scherhant, emphasizing that their collective effort defines the modern German team.

This emphatic victory is significant because it propelled Germany into the tournament's knockout stages through a dominant display of attacking football against a major rival. For Klopp and his squad, the performance validates their tactical evolution under his leadership and injects massive momentum heading into the next phase of the competition, while providing valuable lessons for a transitioning Dutch squad.

stories.title: کراچی کے علاقے گڈاپ میں پارکو آئل لائن سے تیل چوری پکڑی گئی
stories.summary:
کراچی کے علاقے گڈاپ میں پولیس نے سرکاری پارکو آئل لائن سے کروڈ آئل چوری کرنے والے پانچ ملزمان کو گرفتار کرلیا ہے۔ پولیس کے مطابق ملزمان نے آئل لائن تک رسائی حاصل کرنے کے لیے تقریباً دو سو فٹ طویل ایک خفیہ سرنگ بنا رکھی تھی۔ اس سرنگ کے ذریعے پائپ لائن میں لوہے کا کلپ لگا کر پریشر پائپ اور پلاسٹک کا پائپ جوڑا گیا تھا تاکہ تیل نکالا جا سکے

کارروائی کے دوران ملزمان چوری شدہ تیل کو ٹینکروں میں منتقل کر رہے تھے، جنہیں پولیس نے رنگے ہاتھوں پکڑ لیا۔ پولیس نے موقع سے ایک آئل ٹینکر اور ایک ٹرک بھی برآمد کر لیا ہے، جبکہ چوری شدہ تیل کی سپلائی کے حوالے سے مزید تفتیش کا سلسلہ جاری رکھا گیا ہے

یہ کارروائی شہر میں تیل چوری کے بڑھتے ہوئے واقعات کی روک تھام کے لیے کی گئی اہم کارروائیوں کا حصہ ہے۔ پولیس اس بات کی بھی جانچ کر رہی ہے کہ اس غیر قانونی نیٹ ورک میں کون کون سے دیگر افراد ملوث ہیں اور یہ تیل کہاں سپلائی کیا جا رہا تھا

stories.title: Carlos Alcaraz Dominates Frances Tiafoe in Straight Sets at Turin
stories.summary:
Carlos Alcaraz opened his campaign at the ATP Finals in Turin on Monday with a commanding straight-sets victory over American Frances Tiafoe, winning 6-2, 6-2. The world number three needed just over an hour to dismantle his opponent at the Palasport Olimpico, displaying the speed and power that make him a tournament favorite after finishing as the runner-up last year. Alcaraz has enjoyed a strong run since returning in August from a four-month wrist injury layoff, capturing three titles out of five tournaments, most notably the Paris Masters.

Tiafoe struggled to find answers during his debut match at the season-ending championship, though he briefly threatened in the second set when he squandered three break opportunities while trailing 3-2. Alcaraz controlled nearly every facet of the game, expressing comfort and confidence in his overall form. With this win, the 25-year-old Spanish player can secure an early berth in the semi-finals if he defeats local favorite Flavio Cobolli on Wednesday. In other tournament action, Cobolli later lost 7-6, 6-3 to fourth-ranked Daniil Medvedev.

Away from the court, Alexander Zverev was presented with his official ATP year-end World No 1 trophy in Turin. Zverev celebrated a historic season that included Grand Slam titles at Roland Garros and the US Open, alongside a Tour-leading 66 victories. Zverev enters his upcoming match against American Ben Shelton carrying immense momentum, reflecting a stellar year of career-best achievements.

This early round victory matters because it establishes Alcaraz as the man to beat in Turin as he pursues his first ATP Finals title. Demonstrating top-tier physical and mental form following his injury recovery, Alcaraz has positioned himself ideally to advance deep into the tournament while setting up high-stakes matches against the world's best tennis players.

stories.title: Portugal Coach Jorge Jesus Defends Team Amid Ronaldo Retirement Fallout
stories.summary:
Portugal coach Jorge Jesus expressed frustration during a press conference in Cardiff on November 16, 2026, over persistent questioning regarding Cristiano Ronaldo’s international retirement. The inquiry follows Portugal's 4-1 defeat to Denmark, a result that drew public criticism from Ronaldo’s mother, Dolores Aveiro, who stated she was pleased to see Jesus experience his first loss since taking charge after the World Cup. Aveiro claimed Ronaldo had been deceived by the manager, keeping media attention heavily focused on the legendary forward ahead of Portugal's final Nations League group match against Wales.

Ronaldo, aged 41, announced his retirement from international football earlier in the month following a breakdown in his relationship with Jesus, whom he had also played under at Saudi club Al-Nassr. The dispute began after Jesus asked Ronaldo to warm up during a September match against Norway without bringing him on as a substitute. Although Ronaldo briefly left the team camp, received a suspension and fine, and later apologized, he ultimately chose to conclude a legendary 23-year international career featuring world-record marks of 234 appearances and 146 goals. Despite his historic status, critics had frequently cited his diminished mobility as a limiting factor for Portugal in major tournaments.

Prior to the heavy loss to Denmark, Jesus's squad had achieved four consecutive victories. The manager urged his players to move past the setback and concentrate on securing at least a point against Wales in Cardiff to guarantee top spot in Group A4. Meanwhile, Wales boss Craig Bellamy weighed in on the situation, defending Ronaldo's legacy and noting that the football world will genuinely miss one of the game's greatest competitors.

This ongoing controversy matters because it highlights the lingering turbulence surrounding the national team during a critical transitional phase. Dealing with heavy media scrutiny, external criticism from Ronaldo's family, and the pressure to secure group leadership in the UEFA Nations League, Jorge Jesus must quickly refocus his squad on team cohesion and performance on the pitch.

stories.title: Islamabad to Host Top-Level Makkah Defense Alliance Summit This Month
stories.summary:
Pakistan is scheduled to host a high-level security committee meeting for the Makkah defense agreement later this month in Islamabad. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar announced during a press briefing that the upcoming gathering will bring together officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye to advance their joint security framework.

The trilateral pact, initially signed on August 7 in Makkah, establishes a collective security mechanism where an armed attack against any single member is treated as an aggression against all three signatories. Citing Article 51 of the United Nations Charter, Dar emphasized that the pact relies on the principle of collective self-defense and aims to foster regional peace rather than provoke conflict.

Institutional development for the alliance has progressed since its inaugural meeting in Istanbul on August 31, with plans to establish an implementation working committee consisting of foreign office, military, and administrative representatives. The agreement features strict confidentiality rules, prohibits early withdrawal during its initial decade, and emphasizes mutual cooperation in intelligence sharing, counterterrorism, and defense manufacturing.

The upcoming Islamabad summit follows an emergency meeting held in Riyadh, where the three nations discussed the rapid deployment of military capabilities to protect Saudi Arabia from Houthi rebel attacks originating from Yemen. These regional tensions coincide with broader Middle Eastern conflicts involving Iran, US-Israeli strikes, and recent security incidents in Bahrain and the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: امریکا شرائط تسلیم کرے تو آبنائے ہرمز کھول سکتے ہیں: عباس عراقچی
stories.summary:
ایرانی وزیر خارجہ عباس عراقچی نے کہا ہے کہ اگر امریکا تہران کی پیش کردہ شرائط تسلیم کرلے تو اہم عالمی بحری گزرگاہ آبنائے ہرمز کو صرف 48 گھنٹوں کے اندر دوبارہ کھولا جا سکتا ہے۔ انہوں نے اس بات کا اعادہ کیا کہ تہران ہمیشہ سے سفارتی حل کے لیے تیار ہے اور واشنگٹن کی طرف سے شرائط ماننے پر اس معاملے میں مزید تاخیر نہیں کی جائے گی۔

اسلام آباد میں صحافیوں سے گفتگو کرتے ہوئے ایرانی وزیر خارجہ نے جنگ کے خاتمے کے لیے پاکستان کی ثالثی کی کوششوں پر اطمینان کا اظہار کیا۔ انہوں نے بتایا کہ اقتصادی تعاون تنظیم (ای سی او) کے رکن ممالک نے امریکا کے ساتھ جاری جنگ ختم کرنے اور آبنائے ہرمز کو دوبارہ کھولنے کے لیے ایران کے پیش کردہ منصوبے کی بھرپور حمایت کی ہے۔

عباس عراقچی نے ای سی او وزارتی کونسل کے 30 ویں اجلاس سے خطاب کرتے ہوئے خطے میں تجارت، مواصلاتی روابط اور توانائی کے شعبوں میں باہمی تعاون کو مزید مضبوط بنانے پر زور دیا۔ ان کا کہنا تھا کہ رکن ممالک کے مابین اشتراک کار بڑھانا خطے کے مشترکہ مفادات اور معاشی استحکام کے لیے انتہائی ناگزیر ہے۔
انہوں نے مزید کہا کہ علاقائی تعاون کے فروغ سے بیرونی خطرات اور غیر ملکی انحصار میں کمی لائی جا سکتی ہے۔ ایک جدید تجارتی معاہدہ اس خطے کے عوام کے لیے نئے اقتصادی مواقع پیدا کرنے میں معاون ثابت ہوگا۔

stories.title: Nvidia Board Rules Out Jensen Huang's Return Amid Massive Campaign
stories.summary:
Nvidia's board of directors is not considering bringing back Jensen Huang as CEO, despite a massive public and employee campaign demanding his reinstatement. Huang resigned from his position last Thursday following reports of alleged affairs with employees, including a direct report. His departure triggered a crisis for the artificial intelligence chip giant and led to a groundswell of support, highlighted by a petition with over 180,200 signatures.

Prominent figures, including Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, and US President Donald Trump, have expressed support for Huang's return or indicated they would not oppose it. Additionally, thousands of individuals identifying as current Nvidia employees and shareholders joined the online "Stand With Jensen" push. The adulation was particularly prominent in Taiwan, where Taipei 101 was illuminated with messages supporting him, reflecting his immense popularity in the region that houses critical manufacturing partners like TSMC.

Despite the widespread backing, governance experts, institutional investors, and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have urged caution or advocated for an outsider to take over. Critics warn that reinstating Huang before ongoing investigations are complete could introduce significant legal and operational risks. US intelligence agencies are currently examining the nature of Alice Huang's relationship with China's Ministry of State Security to determine what information she may have shared.

The succession dilemma and governance uncertainty have weighed on the company, causing Nvidia shares to fall 3.7 percent on Monday ahead of its third-quarter earnings report. While some investors argue that Huang's vital relationships with key customers and suppliers make his return essential, institutional stakeholders remain largely risk-averse as the probes continue.

stories.title: شدید دھند کے باعث موٹروے ایم 4 پنڈی بھٹیاں سے عبدالحکیم تک بند
stories.summary:
لاہور اور اس کے گردونواح میں شدید دھند کے باعث موٹروے ایم 4 کو پنڈی بھٹیاں سے عبدالحکیم تک ہر قسم کی ٹریفک کے لیے مکمل طور پر بند کر دیا گیا ہے۔ موٹروے پولیس کے ترجمان کا کہنا ہے کہ راستوں کی یہ بندش مسافروں کی جان و مال کے تحفظ کو یقینی بنانے کے لیے کی گئی ہے۔

موٹروے پولیس نے عوام اور ڈرائیورز کو ہدایت کی ہے کہ وہ دھند کے اس موسم میں غیر ضروری سفر سے گریز کریں اور دن کی روشنی کو ترجیح دیں۔ ترجمان نے مشورہ دیا ہے کہ مسافر صبح 10 بجے سے شام 6 بجے کے درمیان سفر کریں، کیونکہ اس دوران دھند کے اثرات نسبتاً کم ہوتے ہیں۔

دہشت گردی اور حادثات سے بچنے کے لیے ڈرائیورز کو تاکید کی گئی ہے کہ وہ دورانِ سفر گاڑی کی رفتار کم رکھیں اور اگلی گاڑی سے محفوظ فاصلہ برقرار رکھیں۔ اس کے علاوہ لین کی سختی سے پابندی کرنے، اچانک بریک لگانے سے گریز کرنے اور فوگ لائٹس کے ساتھ ہیڈ لائٹس، بیک لائٹس اور وائپرز کو درست حالت میں رکھنے کی بھی ہدایت کی گئی ہے۔

stories.title: Technical Glitch Delays Transactions at Major US Banks
stories.summary:
Several major financial institutions in the United States experienced technical issues on Monday, resulting in delayed transactions for customers. Outage-tracking website Downdetector.com flagged reports of disruptions affecting prominent lenders, including JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, US Bank, and Wells Fargo.

A spokesperson for JPMorgan Chase confirmed that a technical issue caused some transactions to take longer than usual to complete. However, the bank assured customers that they still maintained full access to their accounts and funds, and stated that teams were working quickly to resolve the problem.

According to a source cited by CNBC, there was no indication that bad actors were involved in the JPMorgan incident. Furthermore, sources noted no sign that a software bug or security breach was simultaneously affecting multiple banking institutions.

When contacted by Reuters regarding the Downdetector data, representatives from the other listed banks reported that they were not experiencing any significant operational issues. The technical difficulties prompted immediate monitoring across the financial sector as institutions worked to normalize transaction speeds.

stories.title: بلاول بھٹو کو مستقبل میں وزیراعظم دیکھ رہی ہوں، فریال تالپور
stories.summary:
پاکستان پیپلزپارٹی کی رہنما فریال تالپور نے لاہور میں صحافیوں سے گفتگو کرتے ہوئے کہا ہے کہ وہ بلاول بھٹو کو وزیراعظم کے منصب پر فائز ہوتے دیکھ رہی ہیں۔ انہوں نے اس موقع پر زور دیا کہ پنجاب کے اندر آج بھی پیپلزپارٹی کے لیے سیاسی میدان اور گنجائش موجود ہے، اس لیے جماعت کو آئندہ بلدیاتی انتخابات کی بھرپور انداز میں تیاری کرنی چاہیے۔

اپنی گفتگو کو آگے بڑھاتے ہوئے انہوں نے اپنے ماضی کا ذکر کیا کہ وہ اپنے والد کی کمپنی کی ڈائریکٹر تھیں لیکن اس کے باوجود انہیں پابند سلاسل کیا گیا، اور اس بات کا اظہار کیا کہ خواتین کو جیل کی سلاخوں کے پیچھے نہیں ہونا چاہیے۔

شہر قائد کے حوالے سے گفتگو کرتے ہوئے فریال تالپور کا کہنا تھا کہ کراچی ایک بہت وسیع و عریض شہر ہے اور وہاں انتظامی و ترقیاتی حوالے سے بے شمار کام کیے گئے ہیں۔ اس کے برعکس انہوں نے سوالیہ انداز میں پوچھا کہ کیا جنوبی پنجاب اتنی ہی ترقی یافتہ حالت میں ہے جتنا کہ لاہور شہر ہے؟
